The mighty angel signifies our Lord Jesus Christ, of whom the Psalmist says: “The Lord is strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle” (Ps. 24:8). He is said to descend from heaven clothed with a cloud because our Lord, coming into the world, put on flesh, which is signified by the cloud, so that through the assumption of flesh he might conform himself to human beings, whom he came to redeem.

By the rainbow his mercy is signified, as we said above; by his head, divinity is understood in this passage. He had a rainbow upon his head because his divinity, before his incarnation, had taken on such great mercy that he did not disdain to become human for human beings and finally to be condemned to a most terrible death.

“And his face was like the sun.” The Lord is often signified by the sun, because the sun surpasses all visible creatures in its splendor and beauty. But what creature could be compared with its Creator? Nevertheless, invisible things are often demonstrated through visible figures.

In the heart of the elect, therefore, Christ is the sun. They never cease to behold him through hope, and they believe that they will attain the vision of his beauty.

“And his feet were like pillars of fire.” By the pillar of fire we may understand the Church, either because she shines, kindled by the Holy Spirit, or because she burns without ceasing with love of God and neighbor.[^c0080-10] By the two feet we must understand the two peoples. One pillar is formed from the two feet because one Church of God is built from the two peoples, namely, Jews and Gentiles.

We may also understand by the two feet the two Testaments, as we shall demonstrate more fully in what follows. This does not conflict with the preceding interpretation, since the Old Testament was given especially to the Jews and the New Testament especially to the Gentiles.

### (Verse 2)

“And he held in his hand a little open book.” Above, this Book is described as having been sealed with seven seals; but, with the Lord’s help, we have said something about its opening.

Our Lord Jesus Christ therefore appeared to hold the open little book in his hand because he himself opened the meaning of the divine Scriptures to the teachers of the Church. “And he placed his right foot upon the sea, and his left upon the earth.”

By the right foot, as we said, the New Testament is signified; by the left, the Old Testament. We may understand the Gentile people by the sea, on account of the depth of their ignorance and error; by the earth, which is cultivated so that it may bear fruit, the Jews are signified, because they were cultivated through the discipline of the Law and bore fruit when they fulfilled the legal precepts, although in a carnal manner.

The Lord placed his right foot upon the sea when he delivered the doctrine of the Gospel more particularly to the Gentiles than to the Jews, as Paul says to those same Jews: “It was necessary that the word of God be spoken to you first; but since you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles” (Acts 13:46).

He placed his left foot upon the earth when he delivered the Law especially to the Jews. But let no one be troubled that he has mentioned what came later first and what came first afterward, since this often occurs in the divine Scriptures. To prove this, let us offer only one example.

In Psalm 105, when it had said: “The earth opened and swallowed Dathan, and covered over the assembly of Abiram; and fire blazed in their assembly, flame consumed the sinners” (v. 17), it turns back and says: “And they made a calf at Horeb and worshiped a molten image.” It is therefore not inappropriate that the New Testament is signified by the right foot and the Old Testament by the left, since the Old Testament was a shadow of the New Testament.

### (Verse 3)

“And he cried out as when a lion roars.” Christ cried out through the Law, but not as when a lion roars, because his voice was heard only in the one house of Israel. Later he cried out through the Gospel as when a lion roars, because his voice resounded throughout the whole world.

“And when he had cried out, the seven thunders uttered their voices.” By the seven thunders we may understand the seven virtues. Christ cried out through the Law, but the seven thunders did not sound; he cried out through the Gospel, and the seven thunders uttered their voices.

For those to whom the Law said, “Cursed is anyone who does not leave offspring in Israel,” and to whom, for this reason, it was permitted to have several wives and concubines, had not yet heard the thunder of chastity.

Likewise, those to whom the Law said, “An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth,” and, “Whatever blemish anyone inflicts, the same must he suffer” (Exod. 21:24), had not yet heard the thunder of patience.

Nor had those who heard the Law say, “You shall love your friend, and you shall hate your enemy” (Matt. 5:43), yet perfectly heard the thunder of charity. The same is to be understood of the remaining virtues.

The seven thunders therefore spoke when, through the teaching of the Gospel, the loftiness of the virtues began to be revealed.

### (Verse 4)

“And I heard a voice from heaven saying to me: Seal up the things that the seven thunders have spoken, and do not write them.” The voice from heaven is a voice from the Church. To write is to preach, because just as a writer writes with ink in a book so that readers may be instructed, so any teacher writes the words of God when, by preaching them, he plants them in the hearts of his hearers.

Why, then, did the voice that sounded from heaven forbid that the seven thunders be written? We can find the answer in the Acts of the Apostles and in Paul’s Epistles.

At the beginning of the faith, the holy preachers, seeing the weakness of the Gentiles who were coming to the faith, did not dare to entrust them with the more demanding commandments of Christ, lest, frightened by the severity of the commandments, they should not dare to approach the acceptance of Christ’s faith. Thus the apostle Paul wrote to his disciples: “I gave you milk to drink, not food, as to infants in Christ; for you were not yet able, and indeed you are not yet able, for you are still carnal” (1 Cor. 3:2).

The apostles who were in Jerusalem likewise instructed those who had believed from among the Gentiles, saying: “It has seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to impose no further burden upon you except that you abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from fornication, from what is strangled, and from blood” (Acts 15:28).

The voice from heaven therefore speaks to John, telling him not to write the seven thunders, because the apostles—who are signified by heaven—commanded the first preachers not to force those newly coming to the faith to ascend immediately to the heights of the virtues, until, strengthened in the faith, they could proceed to the practice of the virtues.

### (Verses 5–7)

“And the angel whom I saw standing upon the sea and upon the earth lifted up his hand and swore by him who lives forever, who created heaven and the things in it, and the earth and the things in it, and the sea and the things in it, that time would be no more, but that in the days of the seventh angel, when he begins to sound his trumpet, the mystery of God will be completed, as he proclaimed through his servants the prophets.”

When we swear, we want what we say to be firm. Thus, to say that the Lord swore means that he said what cannot fail, because it is impossible for what God says to be nullified, as he himself says in the Gospel: “Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away” (Luke 21:33).

When Christ therefore swore by him who lives forever and by him who made all creatures, he swore by himself, because “all things were made through him, and without him nothing was made” (John 1:3).

He did not swear by binding himself through certain words, but by declaring what was to come. By the seventh angel, however, the preachers who will exist at the end of the world are signified; we shall speak of them in what follows.

Christ therefore swore that in the days of the seventh angel the mystery of God, which he proclaimed through his prophets, would be completed, because he foretold that the end would come when the full number of the elect had been completed.

### (Verse 8)

“And the voice that I heard from heaven spoke to me again and said: Go, take the book from the hand of the angel who stands upon the sea and upon the earth.” He calls it the first voice when it was said to him from heaven: “Seal up the things that the seven thunders have spoken, and do not write them.” He says that he heard the same voice again because it was the voice of the same Holy Spirit.

By John in this passage we must understand all the apostles. The divine voice therefore spoke to John so that he would go to the angel and receive the book from him, because the grace of the Holy Spirit inspired the apostles to leave everything and follow Christ, so that they might receive the doctrine of the Gospel from him.

### (Verses 9–10)

“And I went to the angel, telling him to give me the book.” The apostles went to Christ to be instructed by him in the doctrine of the divine Scriptures.

“And he said to me: Take it and devour it; it will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be sweet like honey. And when I had devoured it, my stomach became bitter.”

By the mouth, in which flavors are distinguished, we may understand the hearts of the apostles. By the stomach, in which all the body’s impurities reside, we must understand the memory of sins.

When the book was devoured, therefore, it is said to have been sweet like honey, because when the divine Scripture is turned over in the mind and promises eternal life to those who keep God’s commandments, it becomes sweet as honey in the heart.

But when it brings the mind down from higher things to lower ones—that is, from contemplation of the heavenly homeland to consideration of one’s sins—and shows the punishments that the impious will suffer for their sins, what had previously been sweet in its revelation of heavenly glory becomes bitter in its disclosure of sins.

We may also understand this specifically of John, who, before writing the Gospel, was led into exile on Patmos. But because, in his absence, the heretics had invaded the Church of God, after his return from exile he was compelled to write the Gospel in order to destroy their blasphemies.

The divine voice therefore commanded John to go to the angel and receive the book from him because, by inspiring John, the Holy Spirit urged him to go to Christ—not with the steps of the body but with the steps of the mind—to contemplate his divine power and equality with the Father, so that he might write a little book about his divinity, beneficial for all the faithful.

John devoured the book when he received in full the knowledge of the Gospel that he later wrote. When the book was devoured, therefore, it offered the sweetness of honey to the mouth, because the more the divine Scripture is ruminated in the heart, the more health-giving sweetness it offers to the mind.

By the stomach, however, in which food decays, we may understand this mortal flesh. The book, therefore, which was sweet in the mouth produced bitterness in the stomach, because the more holy men devote themselves to meditation on the divine Scriptures, and the sweeter their meditation becomes in the mind, the greater the bitterness they bring to their flesh, afflicting it with fasts, vigils, abstinence,[^c0080-11] and other hardships by which the flesh is worn down.

### (Verse 11)

“And he said to me: You must prophesy again about peoples and nations and languages and many kings.” It is foretold to him that he will return from exile to preach.

But since the holy Fathers report that after his return from exile he preached only at Ephesus and in the surrounding places, and died there and rests there in body, how is he said to have prophesied about peoples, nations, languages, and many kings?

He prophesied—that is, he preached—through his Gospel, which he later wrote for all nations, languages, and many kings. For it was scattered among all nations, and through its meditation all the peoples of the earth, as well as many kings, make progress.

# CHAPTER XI

[^c0080-1]: “Although blessed Gregory … divided [old age]” is defended by the common authority of all the manuscripts.

[^c0080-2]: “So also the devil … and kill the soul” is missing from the Gem. manuscript.

[^c0080-4]: All the editions read: “so that they might fulfill the desires of their flesh”; all the manuscripts read: “so that they might become rich,” etc.

[^c0080-5]: The editions read: “for divine ministries, but for diabolical rites”; the manuscripts read as in the text.

[^c0080-6]: This whole passage should be included in the edition on the authority of the manuscripts.

[^c0080-7]: The editions read: “that is, their preachers”; the manuscripts, more correctly: “that is, their persecutors.”

[^c0080-8]: The editions read as above; the manuscripts instead have: “for by an infinite number…”

[^c0080-9]: Thus the manuscripts; the editions instead read: “that they might not worship idols of gold and silver and gold, etc.”

[^c0080-10]: The editions lacked the words “either because she shines, kindled by the Holy Spirit,” which have been restored from the manuscripts.

[^c0080-11]: The editions read: “abstinence from vices, and other things”; the manuscripts omit “from vices.”

(Verse 1.) “And a reed like a measuring rod was given to me, saying: Rise and measure the temple of God, and the altar, and those worshiping in it.” By the reed with which the ancients used to write, the Gospel that was given to him by the Lord and that he later wrote is signified; by the rod, discipline is often understood. The reed, therefore, that was given to John had the likeness of a rod, because the discipline of Christians is the Gospel. Hence he is commanded to measure the temple, the altar, and those worshiping in it: by the temple, the Church; by the altar, holy and perfect men who stand within the Church; and by those worshiping in it, the rest of the multitude, which is instructed by their teaching, are signified. Indeed, each preacher measures the temple of God, the altar, and those worshiping in it when he administers spiritual teaching to each according to his own capacity. [Col. 0867B] For the wise must be taught in one way, the foolish in another; the educated in one way, the uneducated in another; the pagan in one way, the Christian in another; the heretic in one way, the Catholic in another. For the Lord also says in the Gospel that a householder going abroad called his servants and entrusted his possessions to them. To one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one—to each according to his own ability (Matt. 25:14). [Note: All printed editions read “administers,” adding: “in one way to heretics, in another to Catholics”; but the manuscripts agree with us.]

(Verse 2.) It continues: “But the courtyard that is outside, cast out, and do not measure it, because it has been given to the nations.” If it was outside, how could it be cast outside? By the courtyard, therefore, the Jews are signified. The Jews were outside through unbelief; but John and the other apostles still held them in their hearts through love, as the Apostle Paul says: “I could wish that I myself were accursed from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my kindred according to the flesh, who are Israelites” (Rom. 9:3). Hence he is commanded not to measure it—that is, not to minister to them the words of preaching—as the Lord himself commands in the Gospel, saying: “Do not cast your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and, turning, tear you to pieces” (Matt. 7:6). And the Lord speaks to the prophet Ezekiel, saying: “Behold, I will make your tongue cleave to your palate, and you will not be like a man who rebukes, because it is a provoking house” (Ezek. 7:26). This courtyard is said to have been given to the nations because the Jews, on account of their unbelief, had been joined to the pagan nations; or because they had been handed over to the nations, that is, to the Romans, so that they might be destroyed and exterminated by them. “And they will trample the holy city for forty-two months.” He suddenly turns to Elijah and Enoch, who are to come in the time of Antichrist; and in a sufficiently beautiful order, namely, so that after presenting the Jews’ rejection under the figure of the courtyard, he might silently add their restoration. For it is established that at the end of the world the Jews will return to faith in Christ through the preaching of Elijah and Enoch. Thus Antichrist and his ministers will trample—that is, persecute—the holy city, namely, the Church, for forty-two months, which make three years and a half.

[Col. 0868B] (Verses 3, 4.) “And I will give to my two witnesses, and they will prophesy for 1,260 days, clothed in sackcloth.” The Lord calls Elijah and Enoch his two witnesses; they will precede his second coming, just as John preceded his first. “These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands standing before the Lord of the earth” (Matt. 5:15). The olive produces oil, which is afterward placed upon the lampstand so that it may give light to all who are in the house. By oil in this passage we can understand spiritual wisdom. For each person is an olive tree when, resting in solitude within himself, he strives to serve God through the grace of contemplation; when he strives to fulfill what the Lord says in the Gospel: “Let not your left hand know what your right hand does, so that your alms may be in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you” (Matt. 6:3). A lampstand, however, he becomes when he fulfills what the Lord says in the Gospel: “Let them see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven” (Matt. 5:16).

These two holy men, therefore, are now olive trees when, placed in some region of the earth where the divine majesty has commanded them to dwell, they serve God through the grace of contemplation. They will then become lampstands when they come to fulfill the duty of their preaching, when they proclaim the word of God to all, both the faithful and the reprobate. [Note: The manuscripts agree, except that where some manuscripts and the editions read “office,” Sag. has “mystery,” perhaps for “ministry.” The entire passage appears in the editions as follows: “they will come to the duty [office] of their preaching, when they will proclaim the word,” etc.] Of this lampstand the Lord says in the Gospel: “Nor do they light a lamp and put it under a bushel, but on a lampstand, so that it may give light to all who are in the house” (ibid., 15). The lamp is placed upon the lampstand when the duty of preaching is entrusted to a holy man who illumines the good that he preaches with the flames of good works. But the lamp is placed under a bushel [Col. 0868D] when the duty of preaching is entrusted to some reprobate who governs by evil works the good that he preaches, so that he does not provide light to those who are in the house, as Saint Gregory says: when a person’s life is despised, it remains that his preaching too will be despised. [Note: The editions add, “as it is written”; all the manuscripts instead restore this corruption rather than a mere lapse.] Therefore the two olive trees and the two lampstands are said to stand before the Lord because, placed on earth, they await the time when they will fulfill the duty of their preaching and pay the debt of death, as what follows makes clear.

(Verse 5.) “And if anyone wishes to harm them, fire will come out of their mouth and devour their enemies; and if anyone wishes to injure them, so must he be killed.” Since the Holy Spirit speaks through the mouths of the saints, as the Lord says in the Gospel: “For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you” (Matt. 10:20), the words of the saints are not inappropriately called fire, as the Psalmist says of the Lord: “Your word is thoroughly tested by fire, and your servant has loved it” (Ps. 118:140). Fire, therefore, will come out of the mouths of these saints and devour their enemies, because their teaching will destroy the errors of Antichrist so completely that, to all who possess sound minds, nothing that Antichrist and his ministers will attempt to assert will appear defensible. What follows—“And if anyone wishes to injure them, so must he be killed”—pertains to the same matter.

(Verse 6.) “They have power to shut the heavens, so that rain may not fall during the days of their prophecy; and they have power over the waters, to turn them into blood, and to strike the earth with every plague as often as they wish.” We read that Elijah shut the heavens by prayer and opened them again; and Moses also turned waters into blood. Therefore one must not suppose that Elijah will possess less power when he comes to fulfill the duty of his preaching than he possessed when he lived among human beings, but rather greater power. We can also understand the Church by heaven and the words of the saints spiritually by rain. Heaven is closed to the wicked when God, in his judgment, permits their hearts to be hardened in such a way that they offer no access at all to the word of God into their hearts, so that they may be saved.

The prophet Isaiah also shut heaven to the Jews when the Lord said to him: “Make the heart of this people blind, and make their ears heavy, and close their eyes, lest they see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and be converted and I heal them” (Isa. 6:10). Jeremiah also shut heaven to his enemies when he said to the Lord: “Do not be favorable to their iniquity, and let not their sin be blotted out from your sight. Let them fall before you; at the time of your visitation they will perish” (Jer. 18:23). [Note: All the editions read “Jeremiah to his friends”; all the manuscripts, better, read “Jeremiah to his enemies.”] Did Moses not have the power to shut and open heaven, when the Lord said to him after the people had sinned: “Let me alone, so that my wrath may burn against them and I may destroy them, and I will make you into a great nation” (Exod. 32:10)?

Those saints, then, will close heaven to some, so that the rain of God’s mercy may not descend upon them—namely, those whom they will not have been able to recall from the errors of Antichrist. But they will open it to others—namely, those whom they will have recalled from the errors of Antichrist—and will rain upon them, when by their prayers they make God favorable toward them. [Col. 0870A] By the waters that they are said to turn into blood, peoples are signified; blood, however, demonstrates divine vengeance. Thus they will turn waters into blood when they decree in their judgment that the nations that have departed from faith in Christ are to be condemned to everlasting death.

(Verse 7.) “And when they have finished their testimony, the beast that rises from the abyss will make war against them, and will conquer them, and kill them.” This beast signifies Antichrist. He will make war against them when he persecutes them; but he will conquer them not by overcoming them in argument, but by killing them.

(Verse 8.) Hence it continues: “And he will kill them, and their bodies will lie in the street of the great city, which is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, where their Lord also was crucified.” If we wish to understand the earthly Jerusalem by the great city because it says, “where their Lord also was crucified,” we will depart from the truth; for that Jerusalem was destroyed down to its foundations, and the one built in its place is said to have been situated not in the same place but in another. Nor should it be called Sodom and Egypt, since it is inhabited by Christians. At the same time, we must consider that wherever “the great city” occurs in this book, it signifies Babylon, which is the city of the devil and consists of all the reprobate.

As for the statement that their bodies are to be cast into the street of the great city, we can understand it simply, so that they lie in whatever street belongs to the jurisdiction of some reprobate. But it seems better to me that, just as we have said that all the reprobate are to be understood by the great city, so by the street we should understand the hearts of the reprobate. The bodies of the saints, therefore, will lie in the street of the great city, because the saints lie among those by whom they are regarded as entirely insignificant; whereas they stand upright before the faithful, who behold with the eyes of their hearts how great their virtue and glory are.

The city of the devil is appropriately called Sodom and Egypt, because Sodom is interpreted as “blindness” and Egypt as “darkness.” For who suffers worse blindness and darkness than the wicked, who, rushing headlong so that they may be plunged into the sewer of hell, do not cease hastening by doing evil? In the street of the great city, where the Lord was crucified, the bodies of the saints are described as being cast, because just as Christ was crucified by the members of the devil, so these two prophets will be killed by the same people.

(Verses 9–12.) “And peoples, tribes, languages, and nations will see their bodies for three and a half days, and they will not allow their bodies to be placed in tombs. And those dwelling on the earth will rejoice over them and celebrate, and they will send gifts to one another, because these two prophets tormented those who dwelt on the earth. And after three and a half days the spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet, and great fear fell upon all who saw them. And they heard a loud voice from heaven saying to them: ‘Come up here.’ And they ascended into heaven in a cloud, and their enemies saw them.”

If this is fulfilled according to the historical sense, it is unknown to human beings, but everything is known to God. We can also add a spiritual understanding to this history; but it seems rash to wish to adorn with spiritual meanings that history which we understand. When we stand outside a house, we cannot adorn its interior; but lest we appear to have been entirely silent, let us say a few things.

By the three and a half days we can understand three years and a half, during which these two prophets will preach; by the tombs we can understand the minds of the reprobate. The Lord speaks of these tombs, saying: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, because you are like whitewashed tombs, which outwardly indeed appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of every impurity and the bones of the dead” (Matt. 23:13). “So you also outwardly indeed appear righteous to human beings, but inwardly you are full of robbery and iniquity.” The reprobate, therefore, will not allow the bodies of the saints to be placed in tombs, because they will cast their teaching out of their minds.

The statement that after three and a half days the spirit of life from God will enter into them and that they will stand upon their feet can be understood as referring to the time of the resurrection, which will occur after three and a half periods—not immediately, perhaps, but nevertheless soon afterward. They will stand upon their feet when, after the time of the resurrection, the greatness of their virtue and majesty is revealed to all the wicked. Great fear will fall upon their enemies when they see them, because on the day of judgment, when they see them and their glory, they will be thrown into dreadful fear, saying: “These are the ones whom we once held in derision and made a reproachful example. We fools considered their life madness and their end without honor. How have they been counted among the sons of God, and how is their lot among the saints?” (Wis. 5:3).

And because the prophet Malachi speaks in the person of the Lord, saying: “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet, who will turn the hearts of fathers toward their children” (Mal. 4:5), together with the rest that follows, we believe that the Jews will be converted to faith in Christ through the preaching of Elijah, as we demonstrated above as best we could. [Note: All the editions read, “as we demonstrated above”; all the manuscripts instead read, “as in the body,” that is, “as in the main text.”]

We can also understand by the two witnesses the preachers of the two peoples, namely, of the Jews and of the nations. They are said to prophesy for 1,260 days because throughout the entire time during which the persecution and deception of Antichrist rage throughout the whole world, they will strive to restore to the way of truth as many as they can.

(Verse 13.) “And in that hour there was a great earthquake.” He now returns to the beginning of the preaching of Elijah and Enoch. As we have already said above, an earthquake generally signifies the movement of hearts. An earthquake will occur when, through the preaching of Elijah and Enoch, many are converted to repentance and many to faith.

“And a tenth part of the city fell.” It does not seem to me a sound interpretation to understand the Church by the city whose tenth part fell, since this statement concerns the city of the devil more than the city of God. Therefore he says here that a tenth part of that city fell which above he called the great city, Sodom, and Egypt, and in whose street the bodies of the saints are said to lie unburied for three and a half days.

And because the number ten often signifies the Law, since the Law was received through the Decalogue, by the tenth part that fell we can understand the Jews who observe the Law. When they receive faith in Christ through the preaching of Elijah, they will fall away from and be cut off from the city of the devil.

“And seven thousand persons were killed in the earthquake, and the rest were thrown into fear, and they gave glory to the God of heaven.” Just as the number ten signifies the Law, so the number seven often signifies the grace of the Gospel. Behold: the tenth part of the city, which we have taught consists not of stones but of human beings, fell; yet not ten thousand but seven thousand are reported to have died. The number ten, therefore, has been changed into seven, because the Jews, rejecting legal observances, will receive the teaching of the Gospel, which is represented by the number seven because of the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit.

Thus seven thousand are described as having died because they will die to the devil so that they may live to God. But the rest who were thrown into fear signify the other elect, who, seeing the conversion of the Jews and the divine Scripture fulfilled in them, will advance in the fear and love of God and will not cease praising God for their conversion.

(Verse 14.) “The second woe has passed; behold, the third woe is coming quickly.” The third woe pertains to those evils that the devil will bring about through Antichrist, and to the day of judgment. Since above he says that the angel whom he saw standing upon the sea and upon the earth swore by the one who lives forever that, in the days of the seventh angel, when he begins to sound the trumpet, the mystery of God that he announced through his servants the prophets would be completed, he wished to insert a brief mention of the day of judgment and afterward return to narrating the evils of Antichrist.

If we examine this carefully, we will see that he did this in an orderly fashion. For we know that the holy preachers who are to arise at the end of the world will preach that the day of the Lord is near, so that those whom they cannot bring back to the way of truth by exhortations they may at least summon to repentance by terrors. And because the day of judgment will begin to be preached before the persecutions of Antichrist, John wished to place that same day of judgment before he came, in his narrative, to the persecutions of Antichrist himself.

(Verse 15.) “And the seventh angel sounded his trumpet.” By the seventh angel, as we have said, the holy preachers who are to arise at the end of the world are signified. They will sound the trumpet when they announce the word of God. “And loud voices arose in heaven, saying.” By heaven we can understand the Church; by the loud voices, the words of the saints, who will rejoice at the Lord’s coming for judgment, as the Lord says in the Gospel: “Look up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near” (Luke 21:28).

“The kingdom of this world has become [the kingdom] of our Lord and of his Christ, and he will reign forever and ever.” Was not the kingdom of this world previously the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ? But he called human beings the kingdom of this world, in whose minds either God reigns or the devil reigns. God reigns in his saints; the devil reigns in those who belong to his side, for he is king over all the sons of pride (Job 41:25). The kingdom of this world, therefore, will become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ when the devil, together with all whom he has deceived, has been plunged into hell; when what the angel says to Daniel is fulfilled: “The kingdom and the power that are under the whole heaven will be given to the people of the saints, and they will possess it forever and ever” (Dan. 7:27).

(Verse 16.) “And the twenty-four elders who sit before God upon their thrones fell upon their faces and worshiped God, saying.” By the twenty-four elders in this passage we can understand the souls of the saints who dwell with the Lord in heavenly blessedness; the thrones signify everlasting rest. The twenty-four elders sit before God upon their thrones because the souls of the saints, without their bodies, now rest with the Lord in heavenly blessedness. They fell upon their faces and worshiped because, when the saints of God see God’s most just judgment being carried out and his ineffable power, they will cast themselves down in humble submission before their Creator, knowing that whatever exists is nothing in comparison with the one who is God.

(Verses 17, 18.) “We give you thanks, Lord God Almighty, who are and who were, the Holy One, and who have taken your great power and have reigned. And the nations were angry, and your wrath came, and the time came for the dead to be judged, and to give reward to your servants the prophets, and to the saints and those who fear your name, small and great, and to destroy those who corrupted the earth.” [Note: The Roman edition had cut away the words “and to repay the reward … those who corrupted the earth.”]

Christ now, after assuming human nature, possesses the same holiness as the Father, the same eternity, and the same power; and he existed before he assumed human nature, equal to the Father in all things. But he took his great power when, through his passion, he conquered the devil; and he reigned when he subjected the human race to himself. The nations were angry because wicked people persecuted the Church of God in order to extinguish the name of Christ from the world. But the wrath of God will come when the day of judgment arrives. The time will come for the dead to be judged—that is, for the dead to be judged: those dead who, while placed in this life, did not fear to kill their souls by living wickedly.

“And to give reward to your servants the prophets, and to the saints and those who fear your name, small and great.” This will be fulfilled when on the day of judgment he will say: “Come, blessed of my Father, receive the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world” (Matt. 25:34). He calls “small” those who possess lesser merit, and “great” those who obtain greater grace with God.

“And to destroy those who corrupted the earth.” He calls the wicked corrupters of the earth. This will be fulfilled when he says: “Go, accursed, into the eternal fire, [Note: Restored from the manuscripts: “which has been prepared for the devil,” etc.] which has been prepared for the devil and his angels” (ibid., 41).

But we must ask what earth the wicked corrupted. They certainly corrupted themselves by living wickedly, when they nourished their bodies in luxuries and other vices. They also corrupted the earth of others—namely, those whom they dragged by words and examples into the practice of evil deeds. He now returns to the matters he had passed over, namely, to narrating the evils of Antichrist. And in order to arrive more conveniently at their description, he begins with the coming of Christ, and, recalling the evils that the Church suffered from the devil, he adds how that same devil attempts to overthrow the same Church through Antichrist.

(Verse 19.) “And the temple of God in heaven was opened, and the ark of his covenant was seen in his temple.” We can understand blessed Mary by the temple of God, and by the ark of the covenant, Christ, who assumed flesh from her. The temple of God is not said to have been opened because the womb of the blessed virgin Mary was opened in giving birth to the Lord—for she was a virgin before childbirth, a virgin in childbirth, and a virgin after childbirth—but it is said to have been opened because through her our Lord Jesus Christ was made visible to us.

We can also understand the Old Testament by the temple, and the sacraments concerning Christ contained in the Old Testament by the ark. When Christ came in the flesh, the Old Testament was opened, and the spiritual understanding that lay hidden in it was revealed to the faithful.

“And there were flashes of lightning, and voices, and an earthquake, and a great hailstorm.” By the flashes of lightning, the miracles performed through Christ are signified; by the voices, his preaching. The earthquake signifies the movement of hearts. For many were moved through Christ’s preaching to undertake repentance for their sins: they were moved from unbelief to faith and from evil to good. [Note: Thus the manuscripts; the editions read: “they were moved through faith from unbelief . . . to good through good conversion.”] And because hail usually strikes the earth, by hail we can understand the threats of eternal fire, which are often found in the Gospels; by these the hearts of the wicked are struck so that they may come to their senses and turn away from their iniquities.

## CHAPTER XII

(Verse 1.) “And a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon beneath her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars.” This woman signifies the Church. It was fitting that after Christ’s preaching her form should be described, since Christ’s preaching brought her into being.

We can also understand the present world by heaven in this passage; by the great sign, the great salvation that Christ’s coming and preaching brought to the world; and by the sun, Christ, as the prophet says: “But for you who fear the name of the Lord, the sun of righteousness will rise, and healing is in his wings” (Mal. 4:2).

The woman, therefore, was clothed with the sun because the faithful, from whom the Church consists, put on Christ in baptism, as the Apostle says: “All of you who were baptized into Christ have put on Christ” (Gal. 3:27). By the moon, which she was seen to have beneath her feet, and which waxes and wanes, we can understand this world, which the Church tramples by despising it so that she may pursue heavenly things more freely.

But because the moon illuminates the night, it seems better to me that by the moon we should understand Sacred Scripture, without whose light we cannot walk along the paths of righteousness during the night of this age. Of this light the Psalmist says: “Your word is a lamp for my feet and a light for my paths” (Ps. 118:105). The woman, therefore, was seen to have the moon beneath her feet because the Church, fixing the steps of her mind upon the commandments of the divine Scriptures, knows how to advance daily toward heavenly things.

She was also seen to have upon her head a crown of twelve stars. Christ is the head of the Church, while the twelve stars are the twelve apostles. Nevertheless, by the head we can also understand the minds of the faithful. The woman, therefore, was seen to have a crown of twelve stars upon her head because the doctrine and works of the apostles adorn the minds of the faithful when they strive to imitate them.

(Verse 2.) “And she was with child, and she cried out in labor and was in anguish to give birth.” Just as an infant is formed in the womb, receives human shape and breath, so also the Church nourishes the unbelievers whom she carries in her womb through preaching, until they receive human form—that is, until they believe in Christ and receive the spiritual soul that is given in baptism, when they become children of God.

Hence she is said to cry out in labor and to be in anguish to give birth. The Church cries out by preaching; she also cries out by beseeching God for the salvation of her hearers. She is in anguish to give birth when she mourns those whom she sees lying in sins, as the Apostle Paul says to his weakened disciples: “My little children, for whom I am again in labor until Christ is formed in you” (Gal. 4:19). And in the Acts of the Apostles he speaks to the Ephesians, saying: “For three years I did not cease, night or day, to admonish each one of you with tears” (Acts 20:19). And the Psalmist speaks of preachers, saying: “Going forth they went and wept, casting their seeds” (Ps. 125:6).

(Verses 3, 4.) “And another sign appeared in heaven: and behold, a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his heads seven diadems; and his tail dragged a third of the stars of heaven, and cast them upon the earth.” This dragon signifies the devil. Red is a color as though you were to mix blood with saffron-colored dye. The pale color—that is, the saffron color—agrees with the bloody color because, when blood is poured out, it brings death; and pallor covers the entire body of a dying person. Rightly, therefore, the devil is said to have the color of death (Wis. 2:24), because through his envy death entered the world.

By the seven heads, the reprobate whom the devil used to deceive the human race are signified. The diadems signify his royal power, for he is king, as Scripture says, over all the sons of pride (Job 41:5). For just as by the seven horns of the Lamb all the elect are signified, whom we divided into seven groups, so by the seven heads of the dragon the reprobate who opposed them on the way of God are signified.

The first head of the dragon consisted of the reprobate who lived before the flood, whom Scripture calls the sons of human beings, because they became a snare to those who were called the sons of God. The second head of the devil consisted of those who lived after the flood and before the Law—namely, the inventors of idols and various errors through which the human race was deceived. The third head of the devil consisted of those who, after the Law had been given to the people of God, urged them to worship idols. The fourth head of the devil consisted of the false prophets and wicked kings by whom the people of God were so thoroughly deceived that they were led into captivity for their iniquities. The fifth head consisted of the wicked Jews, who both killed the Lord and persecuted his apostles. The sixth head consisted of the persecutors of the Church. The seventh head of the devil will be Antichrist.

What the ten horns signify we will say in what follows, in the passage where the woman, the prostitute, is seen seated upon the scarlet beast (Rev. 17:3). By the tail, which is the end of the body, Antichrist is signified. The tail of the dragon was therefore seen to drag a third of the stars of heaven because Antichrist will deceive many of those whom human beings regarded as elect and who, like stars in heaven, shine in the Church through knowledge and understanding, and he will plunge them into the pit of destruction.

“And the dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she had given birth he might devour her child.” By the woman in this passage we can also understand blessed Mary, since she is the mother of the Church because she gave birth to him who is the head of the Church, and she is the daughter of the Church because she is a most eminent member of the Church. The dragon therefore stood before the woman so that, when she had given birth, he might devour her child, because at the beginning of Christ’s birth he wished to kill him through Herod, his minister (Matt. 2:13). He also stands before the woman—that is, the Church—so that he may destroy by evil persuasion those whom she generates for God through baptism.

(Verse 5.) “And she gave birth to a male child.” Insofar as this pertains to our Lord Jesus Christ, why was it necessary to say that the woman gave birth to a male child, when we all know that our Lord Jesus Christ is male? But insofar as it pertains to the Church, why does he say that she gave birth to a male child, when every day she generates sons and daughters for God from both sexes?

The female sex is weak. Therefore a woman who, having assumed strength of spirit, conquers the devil and strives to please God through good works is appropriately called a man, because although she is female in body, in strength of spirit she is equal to good men. The woman therefore gave birth to a male child because the Church daily gives birth to the members of him whom the blessed virgin Mary gave birth to. Thus there is one male child whom the virgin Mary gave birth to and whom the Church gives birth to every day, because Christ with all his members is one Christ.

“He is to rule all the nations with an iron rod.” This was said above (on chapter 2). “And her child was caught up to God and to his throne.” This was fulfilled when, forty days after he had risen, he ascended into heaven. The children of the Church, that is, the members of Christ, are caught up daily to God and to his throne when after death they are brought to heavenly things.

(Verse 6.) “And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, so that there they may feed her for 1,260 days.” He calls Christ the wilderness. It is called a wilderness because it is alone, deserted by its inhabitants; likewise Christ was deserted by his own, as the Evangelist says: “He came to his own, and his own did not receive him” (John 1:11). And the Lord speaks through the prophet, saying: “I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the nations there was no man with me” (Isa. 63:3).

The woman therefore fled into the wilderness because the apostles and the other disciples, of whom the Church then consisted, abandoned the devil and everything they possessed and followed Christ. By the 1,260 days the time during which Christ preached is signified (Matt. 19:27). Thus the woman is fed for 1,260 days because the apostles and the other disciples, of whom, as we said above, the Church then consisted, were fed by the Lord for three years and a half with the nourishment of the Gospel.

(Verse 7.) “And there was a great battle in heaven: Michael and his angels battled with the dragon.” Since above he briefly included Christ’s birth and preaching, it follows that he should add how Christ conquered the devil through his passion. Michael, whose name is interpreted as “Who is like God?” signifies Christ. The battle took place in heaven—that is, for the sake of heaven—for Michael battled the dragon for the salvation of all the elect. Christ battled for the salvation of the human race by preaching, suffering, and dying.

Michael’s angels battled—that is, Christ’s apostles battled—with the dragon by preaching, performing miracles, and finally dying for the name of Christ. “And the dragon and his angels fought.” The dragon and his angels fought against Michael when the devil and the rest of the multitude of demons stirred up the Jews against Christ so that they might kill him. He also fought against Michael’s angels when he persecuted Christ’s apostles through both Jews and pagans for so long, until he killed them.

### (Verse 8)

And they did not prevail, nor was their place found any longer in heaven. The devil and his ministers did not prevail in conquering Christ or his apostles, because by the very means through which they thought to conquer, they were conquered. For they thought that they had overcome Christ by his death, but through his death his name became renowned throughout the world. They did not prevail, therefore, nor was their place found any longer in heaven, because through the preaching of the apostles and the other saints they were expelled from the hearts of the elect, who are signified by heaven.

### (Verse 9)

And that great dragon was cast down, the ancient serpent who is called the Devil and Satan, who deceives the whole world; and he was cast down to the earth, and his angels were sent down with him. The devil is rightly called a serpent, either because through a serpent he first deceived the human being, or because through the poison of his wickedness he destroyed the human race. The Devil is interpreted as “falling downward”; for he first fell from heaven through pride, and afterward fell when he was cast out by Christ from the hearts of the elect, as the present passage demonstrates. Satan, however, is interpreted as “adversary”; for he is an adversary of God and of all good people. Woe to those for whom the devil is a friend! For the more he is a friend to anyone, the greater torments he inflicts upon that person; the devil’s friendship is indeed miserable.

When it says, “who deceives the whole world,” it uses the present tense for the past. He had deceived the human race, which is signified by the world; but he had lost a large part of it through Christ. The devil and his angels were therefore cast down to the earth, because, having been expelled from the elect, he possessed only the reprobate, who are signified by the earth.

### (Verse 10)

And I heard a loud voice from heaven saying: Now salvation and power and the kingdom of our God, and the authority of his Christ, have come to be. The loud voice from heaven is the voice of the angels rejoicing over the salvation of the human race and praising God, as the Lord says in the Gospel:

> [Note: [Col. 0877D] Codex Gem., “There is joy among the angels of God in heaven.”]

“There is greater joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who have no need of repentance” (Luke 15:7).

By the one sinner we can understand the Gentile people, and by the ninety-nine righteous persons the Jews. They do not reach the number one hundred, because the Law brought no one to perfection (Hebrews 7:19). For there was much greater joy in heaven over the conversion of the Gentiles than over the observances of the Jews.

At the devil’s downfall, therefore, the salvation of believers came to be. They also received the power to conquer the devil, by whom they had previously been overcome.

> [Note: [Col. 0877D] All printed editions: “they were held captive”; all manuscripts: “they were held defeated.”]

The kingdom of our God likewise came to be, because the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit began to reign in those over whom the devil had reigned. The authority of his Christ also came to be, when Christ began to possess those whom the devil had possessed.

For the accuser of our brothers has been cast down, who accused them before the presence of our God day and night. Guilty people are accused before judges when their crimes are brought to light. But before God, who considers not only deeds but also thoughts, how can the devil accuse anyone? We are accused in God’s presence when we sin; and the devil also accuses us when, by evil persuasion, he casts us down into sins.

### (Verse 11)

And they conquered him because of the blood of the Lamb and because of the word of their testimony. They conquered because of the blood of the Lamb, because Christ’s blood-redemption granted the saints the ability to conquer the devil. They also conquered because of the word of their testimony, by preserving the faith they had professed and fulfilling it through their works.

But what follows is very obscure: “And they did not love their souls even unto death.” For how do the saints not love their souls, for whose salvation they endure every arduous and difficult thing? How do they not love their souls, for which they wear themselves down through vigils, fasts, abstinence, and the practice of the other virtues?

If we wish to understand “soul” as the present life, what saint does not love his life, in which he acquires for himself that heavenly glory “which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has any mind been able to comprehend” (1 Corinthians 2:9)? Or who has ever reached that glory without this life? The present life indeed brings great gain to the saints, just as, conversely, it brings great loss to the reprobate.

Nevertheless, in a certain sense the saints are rightly said to hate their life, because, for love of eternal life, the present life becomes distasteful to them, just as the Psalmist lamented:

> “Woe is me, for my sojourning has been prolonged” (Psalm 119:5).

The Lord also says in the Gospel:

> “Whoever loves his soul will lose it; and whoever hates his soul in this world preserves it for eternal life” (John 12:25).

> [Note: [Col. 0879D] The printed editions lacked the passage from “When he says ‘in this world’” through “the lovers of the world”; we have restored it to its proper place from all the manuscripts.]

When he says “in this world,” he shows how we ought to understand this. Whoever, therefore, loves his soul in this world preserves it for eternal life—that is, according to the world, he will lose it. And whoever hates his soul in this world—that is, according to the world—preserves it for eternal life.

The lovers of the world love their souls according to the world, because they would never wish to depart from this present life, so that they might always live in luxury.

> [Note: [Col. 0880D] The printed editions read, “but always live luxuriously here”; the manuscripts read as in the text.]

That rich man loved his soul according to the world who said:

> “Soul, you have many good things stored up for many years; eat, enjoy yourself, and be satisfied” (Luke 12:19).

But the saints, who do not wish to be conformed to this world, as the Apostle says (Romans 12:2), but to be transformed in the renewal of their spiritual understanding; who do not love the world or the things that are in the world; who do not wish to be friends of this world, lest they be made enemies of God; these hate their souls in this world (1 John 2:15)—that is, they do not love them according to the world (James 4:4), but according to God, for whose love they despise all passing things, so that they may preserve their souls for eternal life.

The saints, therefore, did not love their souls unto death: they did not wish to preserve them in the present life by denying Christ, but chose rather to die for Christ’s name, so that they might find them again in eternal life.

### (Verse 12)

Therefore rejoice, heavens, and you who dwell in them. By the heavens and those who dwell in the heavens we can understand the various Churches, which are one. The children of the Church are therefore commanded to rejoice, because by the Lord’s grace they have deserved to be freed from so savage an enemy.

Woe to the earth and the sea, because the devil has come down to you, having great anger, knowing that he has only a short time. By the earth we can understand the Jews, and by the sea the pagans and the other reprobate. 549 Woe, therefore, to the Jews and to the unbelieving nations! Because of the anger the devil has, since he has lost so great a multitude, he rules over the reprobate with such savagery and casts them down into so many crimes that they are in no way worthy to return to the ways of life and be healed.

It also says that the devil knows that he has only a short time, because the nearer he sees the day of judgment approaching, the more cunning he becomes in deceiving human beings.

### (Verse 13)

And when the dragon saw that he had been cast down to the earth, he persecuted the woman who had given birth to the male child. Seeing that the devil had lost a very great multitude of the elect and had been confined within the narrow confines of the hearts of the reprobate, he persecuted the woman—that is, the Church. For he stirred up the Roman emperors and the entire multitude of the ungodly to persecute God’s people.

### (Verse 14)

And two wings of a great eagle were given to the woman, so that she might fly into the wilderness, to her own place, where she is nourished for a time, and times, and half a time, away from the face of the serpent. By the eagle we can understand Christ; the two wings, however, are the two Testaments. Two wings were therefore given to the woman, because the Church received the two Testaments, so that by their teaching she might both escape the devil and ascend daily to her heavenly homeland.

For he calls this homeland the wilderness, just as the Lord also says in the Gospel when he says that he left the ninety-nine sheep in the wilderness and went to seek the one that had gone astray (Luke 15:4).

He calls this homeland the Church’s place, as he himself will say at the judgment:

> “Come, blessed of my Father; receive the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world” (Matthew 25:34).

By “a time, and times, and half a time” the period from Christ’s Passion to the end of the world is signified. During this span of time, therefore, the souls of the saints—that is, the Church—are nourished in heavenly blessedness by the food of the glory of their heavenly homeland.

### (Verse 15)

And the serpent cast from his mouth after the woman water like a river, so that he might cause her to be swept away by the river. The river of water signifies carnal desires. For when the devil saw that the Church could not be cast down by persecutions, but was instead growing and being strengthened, he wished to pour into her a multitude of carnal desires by which, once deceived, she might be drawn back to the performance of evil works.

### (Verse 16)

And the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed the river that the serpent had cast from his mouth. By the earth we can understand the reprobate, who became receivers of the carnal desires by which the devil wished to ensnare the faithful and draw them to himself.

We can also understand Christ by this same earth. And because there is great power in the Lord’s words—for “he spoke, and they came to be; he commanded, and they were created” (Psalm 148:5)—the earth’s mouth may not improperly be understood as his power.

The earth therefore helped the woman—that is, Christ helped the Church—and opened its mouth and swallowed the river that the serpent had cast from his mouth. That is, he opened the bosom of his mercy, and by his power utterly extinguished the river of vices.

### (Verse 17)

And the dragon was angry with the woman, and went away to make war with the rest of her offspring, those who keep the commandments of God and hold the testimony of Jesus. The rest of the Church’s offspring are the elect who are to be born at the end of the world. How the devil will wage this war is revealed in what follows.

### (Verse 18)

And he stood upon the sand of the sea. By the sand of the sea the multitude of the reprobate who will exist at that time is signified.

## Chapter XIII

### (Verse 1)

And I saw a beast rising from the sea, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon its horns ten diadems. This beast signifies Antichrist. Those who are signified by the sand are also signified by the sea: namely, the multitude of the reprobate.

The beast was therefore seen to rise from the sea, because Antichrist will arise from the society of the reprobate. This beast is described as having seven heads and ten horns. Likewise, the dragon was earlier said to have had seven heads, and upon the heads seven diadems. By these, as we said, all the reprobate whom the devil used to deceive the human race were signified.

But this beast is described as having ten diadems not on its heads but on its ten horns. Therefore the ten horns signify the nations that Antichrist will subjugate; the seven heads signify the seven principal vices.

And so that we may better understand what follows, I have decided, in enumerating the vices, to follow Prudentius, who composed an excellent account in verse of the struggle between vices and virtues.

> [Note: [Col. 0881D] All printed editions read: “to follow the footsteps of Prudentius, who excellently discussed in verse the conflict of vices and virtues. For he placed idolatry as the first vice,” and so forth. All the manuscripts, on the contrary, agree with us. Hence it is evident that the copyist of the manuscript which the bishop of Durham submitted to the press was guilty either of gross ignorance or of disgraceful fraud.]

For he placed idolatry as the first vice, lust as the second, anger as the third, pride as the fourth, luxury as the fifth. Although lust is joined to luxury as one member is joined to the body—for this reason the Fathers often used *luxuria* for lust—there is nevertheless a distinction between lust and luxury. He placed avarice as the sixth, and blasphemy or discord as the seventh.

And because Antichrist will easily deceive and associate with himself those who are subject to these vices, the seven vices are rightly signified by the seven heads.

The Lord speaks of these seven vices in the Gospel, saying:

> “When an unclean spirit has gone out from a person, it wanders through dry places, seeking rest and not finding it. Then it says, ‘I will return to my house from which I came.’ And when it comes, it finds it swept and put in order. Then it goes and takes with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and entering in, they dwell there” (Matthew 12:43).

The unclean spirit went out from the person when the devil went out from the Jews, when they received the Law. It wandered through dry places—that is, through the nations of the Gentiles, which were dry because they did not possess the greenness of faith.

It did not find rest there because, when Christ came in the flesh, it lost the Gentiles whom it had long held. It returned to its house from which it had gone out because it returned to possess the Jews, since they did not wish to believe in Christ. It found the house of the Jews vacant because they did not have Christ as a guest.

But we must ask why he said that those minds which did not have God as their inhabitant were swept and put in order. They had been swept for the devil, not for God. For what is clean in God’s sight appears unclean to the devil; and what is unclean to God is clean to the devil.

> [Note: [Col. 0882D] Gill’s edition has this in the body of the text: “for dung appears cleaner to every living creature”; in the margin, however, it reads: “to certain living creatures.” The Roman edition transferred this utterly inept emendation into the text. We present the true reading found in the manuscripts.]

For just as dung appears cleaner to a beetle than any clean and pleasant food, so the devil loves those hearts more which are filled with every vice than those which abound in every virtue.

Brooms are what cleanse a house of refuse. God therefore has his brooms, and the devil has his. God’s brooms are those things that cleanse his house so that he himself may dwell in it: confession of sins, repentance, tears, and almsgiving. The devil’s brooms are those things which, according to him, sweep his house: love of the world, levity of mind, contempt for God’s commandments, and many other things.

The seven spirits whom the devil took with him are the seven principal vices. With these seven attendants, therefore, the devil possesses the Jews to this day.

But it may be asked why these seven principal vices are said to be worse than the devil. They are indeed worse for us than the demons, because the demons attack us from outside, whereas the vices continually battle against us from within. For just as enemies who attack a city from outside are endured more easily because walls are placed between them, than those who, stationed within, are already devastating the city, so demons, who attack from outside, are endured more easily than vices, which unceasingly ravage us within.

And upon its heads were names of blasphemy. Antichrist’s blasphemy will have many names, because he will blaspheme Christ in many ways.

### (Verse 2)

And the beast that I saw was like a leopard, and its feet were like the feet of a bear, and its mouth was like the mouth of a lion. By the leopard, which is said to have various colors, the hypocrisy of Antichrist is signified. Although he will be a most wicked human being, he will disguise himself in various virtues so that he may more easily deceive fools.

By the bear, which is a very cunning animal, his cleverness in deceiving human beings can be indicated. By the lion, likewise, his cruelty in tearing apart God’s people is signified.

And the dragon gave it his power and great authority. The devil will give Antichrist his power, which is wholly evil, because he will dwell in him and through him will accomplish whatever the devil’s wickedness is capable of devising.

But since Scripture says, “There is no authority except from God” (Romans 13:1), how will the devil give Antichrist great authority? God will give Antichrist authority, but he will so turn that authority toward evil that it will be believed—and will in fact be—entirely diabolical.

### (Verse 3)

And I saw one of its heads as though it had been mortally wounded, and its mortal wound was healed. We said above that the seven principal vices are signified by the seven heads of Antichrist. Therefore, by the head that was not killed but appeared as though it had been killed, blasphemy is signified.

We must therefore ask how blasphemy can be said to have been killed, as it were. In the earliest times of the Gospel there were many heretics who tried to undermine the Church’s faith through their errors. But almighty God chose orthodox Fathers, defenders of the Church, from among the children of the Church itself. Filling them with the river of his wisdom, he eradicated all heresies from his Church through their teaching.

Among these were Ambrose, Hilary, Jerome, Augustine, Gregory, and many others, who also produced a great number of books by which all the heresies that existed, and that could exist, were destroyed.

> [Note: [Col. 0883D] All printed editions read, “eradicated. They also,” and so forth. Whatever is inserted here has been restored from all the manuscripts.]

Blasphemy, therefore, is now as though killed, because although there are many who conceive many blasphemies in their minds, they do not dare to utter the evil they have conceived, lest they be disgracefully refuted by the teaching of these men.

This head—that is, blasphemy—will therefore appear dead in the time of Antichrist. But it will be revived by the devil in Antichrist, whom he will inflame to blaspheme Christ to such a degree that he will surpass all blasphemers in his blasphemies.

And the whole earth marveled after the beast. By the earth sinful human beings are signified.

### (Verse 4)

And they worshiped the dragon because he had given authority to the beast; and they worshiped the beast, saying: Who is like the beast, and who can wage war against it? How will they worship the dragon—that is, the devil—whom they will not see? Those who are signified by the earth will worship Antichrist, and in Antichrist the devil, saying that no one is like Antichrist and that no one can be compared with his strength.

### (Verse 5)

And a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies was given to him. It was given—that is, permitted by God—so that he might speak great things about himself, saying that he is the Son of God, and so that he might speak blasphemies against God.

And authority was given to him to act for forty-two months. It seems difficult that in so very short a time—that is, in three and a half years—he could subject all the nations to himself and bring the human race, apart from a few elect, to his worship. There will indeed be many elect, but in comparison with the unbelievers they will be very few.

Yet it may happen that he first subjects all the nations to his rule, and afterward, lifted up in pride, establishes himself as one to be worshiped as God. For, as it seems to me, the period of persecution alone is included in the three and a half years. During it he will labor with all his power, both personally and through his disciples and through the display of miraculous signs, so that all people may offer him the worship of a deity.

Those who wish to resist he will afflict with various unheard-of torments, so that under compulsion they may do what they would refuse to do voluntarily.

### (Verse 6)

And he opened his mouth in blasphemies against God, to blaspheme his name and his tabernacle and those who dwell in heaven. For he will open his mouth to blaspheme God, namely, the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. He will blaspheme God’s name, saying that Christ is not God. He will also blaspheme God’s tabernacle—that is, God’s Church—saying that the Christian religion benefits believers nothing, but brings destruction rather than salvation.

He will also blaspheme those who dwell in heaven—that is, the martyrs and the other saints—saying that they can benefit no one and that everything believers affirm about them is false. 551

### (Verse 7)

And it was given to him to wage war against the saints and to conquer them. He will wage war against the saints, flattering some, terrifying others, and finally inflicting the worst torments upon them, in order to lead them into his errors. But it cannot happen that the elect be led into error. He will conquer them not by overcoming them, but by killing them.

### (Verse 8)

And authority was given to him over every tribe and people and language and nation; and all who dwell on the earth worshiped him. This will be fulfilled literally.

Many will ask why God allows such things to happen, so that Antichrist should deceive the human race so wickedly. He will permit such things for two reasons. For, as he himself says in the Gospel:

> “In those days the love of many will grow cold, and iniquity will abound” (Matthew 24:12).

Human wickedness will indeed grow to such an extent, and they will provoke God to anger so greatly through their crimes, that they will deserve to be subjected to and deceived by so wicked a man, as Scripture testifies:

> “He makes a hypocrite reign because of the perversity of the people” (Job 34:30).

For God will hand them over, as the Apostle says, to a debased mind (Romans 1:28), so that they may do what is unfitting; and they will care about nothing, provided only that they fulfill whatever evil they have conceived.

> [Note: [Col. 0885D] Thus the manuscripts read; the printed edition, however, has: “there will be nothing worse, provided only that,” and so forth.]

By God’s most just permission, therefore, it will happen that, deceived by Antichrist, they will perish more grievously.

God will also permit this for the testing of his elect, so that, just as gold is tested by fire, they too may be tested and examined in the persecutions of Antichrist, as it is written concerning them in Daniel:

> “Many will be chosen and made white and will be tested like gold.”

> [Note: [Col. 0885D] The printed edition reads, “and many will be made white”; the manuscripts read, “and they will be made white, and like gold,” and so forth.]

It continues:

> “Those whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb who was slain from the foundation of the world” (Daniel 12:10).

The book of life is the predestination of almighty God. The reprobate are not written in the book of life because they were not predestined to eternal life.

But we must ask how the Lamb—that is, Christ—can be said to have been slain from the foundation of the world.

### (Verse 9)

For the statement that follows, “If anyone has ears, let him hear,” wherever it is placed in the divine Scriptures, demonstrates that what preceded it is obscure; for it requires the ears of the heart and of understanding.

The Lamb was therefore slain from the foundation of the world because his death was prefigured from the beginning of the human race in the holy Fathers. It was prefigured in the first human being when, while he slept, Eve was made from his rib. Likewise, it was prefigured in Abel, who was killed by his brother Cain. It was also prefigured through Isaac, whom his father offered to the Lord as a burnt offering. Likewise, through Joseph, whom his brothers sold. His death was also prefigured in the various rites of sacrifice.

Therefore, as often as Christ’s death was either prefigured or foretold by the holy Fathers, so often, as it were, the Lamb was slain.

This may also be understood simply as saying not that the Lamb was slain from the foundation of the world, but that the names of the saints were written from the foundation of the world in the Lamb’s book—he who was slain for their salvation.

### (Verse 10)

Whoever leads into captivity goes into captivity; whoever kills with the sword must be killed with the sword. Antichrist, who will lead the Christian people captive from their Creator, will himself be taken captive from the present life and thrust into hell. And because he will kill the souls of many with the sword of his wickedness and kill the bodies of the righteous with a physical sword, he himself will be condemned by the sword of everlasting death.

> [Note: [Col. 0886D] Codex Gem., “Here is the patience,” and so forth.]

Here is the patience and faith of the saints: that is, the patience and faith of the saints will be proved in the persecutions of Antichrist.

### (Verse 11)

And I saw another beast rising from the earth, having two horns like a lamb, and it spoke like a dragon. This beast signifies either one of Antichrist’s disciples, worse than the others, or many who will preach him.

It was seen to rise from the earth because it will arise from the society of the reprobate. It also appeared to have two horns like a lamb. Above we said that all the elect are signified by the Lamb’s seven horns, which we divided into seven parts. By the fifth horn, we said, the Jews who believed in Christ were signified; by the sixth, the Gentiles who likewise believed in Christ.

The beast will therefore have two horns like the Lamb, because it will possess the Jews and the Gentiles by deceiving them. For although many of the Jews will believe in Christ through Elijah’s preaching, the greatest part of them will follow Antichrist, as the Lord says in the Gospel:

> “I have come in my Father’s name, and you did not receive me; another will come in his own name, and him you will receive” (John 5:43).

This beast therefore spoke like a dragon because its words were diabolical. For the devil, who will speak through Antichrist, will himself also speak through his disciples.

### (Verse 12)

And it exercised all the authority of the first beast in its presence. When it says “in its presence,” it means “in its name”; for Antichrist cannot be present in all the places where he will be preached by his followers.

Antichrist will perform miracles by diabolical art, and his disciples will do so as well. But their miracles will be false, not genuine, as the Apostle says:

> “His coming will be according to the working of Satan, with every power and signs and lying wonders” (2 Thessalonians 3:9).

For it is not credible that they could restore to health those whom God had blinded or weakened. Rather, they will secretly harm only those whom they themselves have harmed, and publicly heal them.

Antichrist himself will also display himself to human beings with such splendor that the foolish will believe him to be God, as the Apostle says:

> “So that he takes his seat in the temple, displaying himself as though he were God” (ibid., 4).

[Col. 0886C]

### (Verse 13)

And it made the earth and those who dwell in it worship the first beast, whose mortal wound had been healed. And it performed great signs, so that it even made fire come down from heaven to earth in the presence of human beings.

We read in the book of Job that, by God’s permission, the devil caused fire to come down from heaven and consume Job’s sheep and servants (Job 1:16). What he did there by himself, he will do at the end of time through Antichrist and his followers.

### (Verse 14)

And it deceived those who dwell on the earth because of the signs that were granted to it to perform in the presence of the beast. Nothing deceives the simple so much as the display of signs. Therefore Antichrist’s ministers will easily deceive the multitude of fools through the performance of signs.

Saying to those who dwell on the earth that they should make an image of the beast that had the sword wound and lived—that is, so that Antichrist might be worshiped in images.

When he says that the beast had a sword wound and lived, it may be that Antichrist will pretend, by diabolical art, to die and rise again, so that by this act he may more easily deceive human beings. Simon Magus is said to have done this.

### (Verse 15)

And it was granted to it to give breath to the image of the beast, so that the image of the beast might speak. We have also heard that certain magicians did this: through the art of necromancy they made statues appear to move and speak.

We can understand this in another way. An image has the appearance of a human being, but is not a human being. Likewise, because of the working of powers and signs, Antichrist will be thought to be God, but this will be utterly false. For it cannot happen that a most impious human being possesses any divinity within himself.

Those who consider Antichrist to be God will therefore make an image of Antichrist. But Antichrist’s ministers will give breath to the image of the beast when they compel those who have believed in Antichrist to blaspheme Christ.

And he will cause those who do not worship the image of the beast to be killed. The faithful who refuse to worship Antichrist will be tormented with various punishments and killed. For there will be such tribulation as the Lord said in the Gospel (Matthew 24:21), such as has not been from the beginning and will not be, so that, if it were possible, even the elect would be led into error.

[Col. 0887B]

### (Verse 16)

And he will cause all—small and great, rich and poor, free and slave—to receive a mark on their right hand or on their foreheads. It may be that, just as we have the mark of Christ, namely the cross, by which we are signed, so Antichrist will have his own mark by which those who believe in him will be signed.

We can also understand this in another way. Antichrist’s disciples will be praisers of vices. For they will teach that wine and other riches were created so that human beings might use them abundantly and sufficiently. They will therefore say that God made the genital organs so that human beings might engage in intercourse with women, and that it is wicked for anyone to abstain from sexual relations; all carnal desires, they will teach, are to be fulfilled.
