What vices does **GLUTTONY** produce? 495. Adam lost paradise through food; Esau lost the honor of primogeniture through lentils; Judas cast down the sublime dignity of apostleship through a morsel of bread, 429. See **FOOD**.

## H

**HERETICS** deceive people under the pretext of the Christian name, 453. They strive to corrupt the meaning of the Law and of faith, 107. They teach only under the name of Christ—and why? 122. You will scarcely find one of the founders of heresies who repented of his errors, 561. Many sects of heretics had arisen from the time of the apostles, of which dry branches remain to this day, 111. Nothing is more dangerous than those heretics who dissent from the true faith in only one word, 347. Heretics persecuted the Church of God, 539. Because of their knowledge of the Scriptures, they consider themselves prophets, ibid. They added certain false things to the divine Scriptures and removed certain others, 588. Faith should not rest on human wisdom, and there is no heresy, 327. Heretics, schismatics, and the licentious are expelled from the camp, 9. Their offering, because they do not have the Holy Spirit, benefits not the worship of God but the worship of demons, 326. None of them can possess the Holy Spirit, 326. They are rightly called the seat of the beast, 560. Dathan and Abiram prefigured those who introduce heresies and schisms into the Church, 11. They are compared with foxes, 446.

**HALUS** is interpreted as “labor,” 8. It is the tenth encampment of the children of Israel; and what happened there? 8.

The **HEBREWS** were so called because of Abraham; the letter was changed on account of the sound, so that they would not be called *Abraei* but *Hebraei*, 259. From the same Abraham come both the name and the Hebrew language, ibid. A man thoroughly instructed in all the books of the Hebrews, after receiving faith, became a perfect teacher, 297. The Hebrews sometimes used the Syriac language, but more often Hebrew, in their treatises or offerings for the sake of commendation, 157.

**ENOCH** was carried away in a fiery chariot—that is, by the conveyance of angels—as though even to heaven, 341.

**JEROME** is cited, 564. See **FATHERS**.

**JERUSALEM** is interpreted as “vision of peace,” that is, of God, 510. Jerusalem was destroyed down to the ground; and the one built in its place is said to have been situated elsewhere, 544.

**HILARY.** See **FATHERS**.

Where there is a **HOLOGRAPH**, that is, a document written in one’s own hand, it cannot be called false, 230.

What great **DIGNITY DOES THE HUMAN BEING** possess in his creation, and what does this teach him? 611. Human flesh was worthy, through the Lord Christ, to enter into and share in the substance and fellowship of the holy Trinity, 332. The human being was made lord of creation so that he might serve the Creator’s will, 437. In what respect is he made according to the likeness of God? 612. How is he the image of the Trinity? 611. The one God made one human being, who would bear the image of his unity, 273. He was made for this purpose: to proclaim the rule of the one God, 56. A person’s judgment almost fashions its own nature, so that something is called what he thinks it to be, 72. He receives his name from his action, 45. Under the designation “soul,” the whole human being is signified, 72; and under “flesh,” likewise, ibid. The human being is twofold, in flesh and soul, 69. Through a new kind of piety, death and life operate in one and the same person: death of sins and life of virtues, 413. How did Christ restore the human being to the original image that he had received? 332. The renewed person emerges from fear, receiving the spirit of joy, 305. What is less removed from paganism, so long as one still places some hope in human beings? 121. The implausible origin of a foreign human being lies in an alien land, 52. That is done honorably which is done with peace and discipline, 160.

**HONOR** of great rank ought to be surrounded by still greater care, 360. The height of honors is scarcely maintained without the burden of sin, 489. What good is it to possess honor without fruit? 283. Beware of honors that you cannot retain without guilt, 489. On the day of judgment incorruptible honor and glory will be given, 37.

**HOSANNA**, that is, “save us,” 433.

Why ought we now to offer a **LIVING SACRIFICE**? 94.

If there were no **INNER ENEMIES**, external enemies could do us no harm, 588. First conquer yourself, so that you may be able to conquer another, 418. It is great skill to avoid the ambushes of an enemy within the household, 69.

**HUMILITY** consists in this: a person does not defend even what he knows is owed to him, 255. It is praiseworthy for a person of high rank to humble himself, 317. Let the one who knows himself to be something humble himself, so that he may become greater, 196. Humble yourself in everything, and you will find grace before God, 426. If a Christian is to glory, he should glory in humility, through which one grows before God, 203, 204, 229. Before God humility is glorious, 200, and it nourishes love of God, 519. It commonly bends the proud, 229. What vices does it extinguish? 493.

The **HUNS** claimed Pannonia for themselves, 564.

**HYPOCRISY.** A person who is evil but presents himself as good is worse than one who is openly evil, 301.

## I

How inexcusable are the **IDOLATERS**? 33, 34, 35. Why did Satan invent idolatry? 145. It is the gravest crime and the source of every error, 59. Through it all vices arose in the world, 35. It has everywhere been called fornication, 454. Under the covering of images the devil is worshiped, 145. How rightly is idolatry represented by smoke? 540.

An **IDOL-SACRIFICE** (*idolothytum*) is that which had been consecrated to idols, 507.

An **IDOL** is vanity, 44. Nothing is so hostile to the human being as idols, 186.

**IGNORANCE.** What we do not know is, as it were, behind us, 501; and it is future for us, 586.

The **IMMORTALITY** that the first human being lost through sin will be restored to the just, 575.

At the expense of the flesh, 165.

When the **EMPEROR** is absent, his image possesses authority, 270.

The **WICKED** are rightly called inhabitants of the earth, 537.

The **IMpenitence** of certain people is sharply reproved, 559.

An **INFERIOR** readily does what he sees done by a superior, 29.

The punishment of **HELL** in some way generates the condemned, in whom they are brought to completion, 285. See **CONDEMNED**.

**INFIRMITIES** are sometimes inflicted on bodies because of sin, 292. Christian infirmity is strength, 418.

Do not be reluctant to visit the **SICK**; through them you will become firm in love, 368.

The **UNGRATEFUL** are those who, when God calls, dissent and reject God’s grace, 53.

**ENEMIES** should be summoned to friendship by kindness, 98. What does it mean to love an enemy? 100. In this consists abundant and perfect justice, ibid. The more grievous enemies are, the more necessary reconciliation is, 29.

**INIQUITY** thinks that, because it is strong, it has conquered for a time, 116.

The cause of **INNOCENCE** is more pitiable, 53.

**INTERPOLATORS AND CORRUPTERS OF THE SCRIPTURES**, 289.

What vices does **ENVY** produce? 493.

**ANGER** is a natural impulse that ordinarily ought to contribute to the improvement of the offender, 243. It arises from sin, 50. An angry mind necessarily thinks evil thoughts, 244. People commonly sin through anger, 98. Nothing is so harsh and bitter, 497. In anger no one recognizes what is useful, 249. It is an inconsiderate thing, to such an extent that the angry person sometimes spares not even himself, 274. What sort of anger ought to be directed against offenders? 244.

**ISAAC** was born as a type of the Savior, 80, 125, 226.

God made **ISAIAH** a martyr after he was sawn in two, 458.

**ISRAEL** signifies the birth of the Jews, while Isaac signifies that of Christians, 225.

Did the **ISRAELITES** fast in the wilderness? 422. Why are the journeys, departures, and encampments of the Israelites from the borders of Egypt to the place where Moses died recounted by God’s command? 1. Why are the encampments of the children of Israel counted as forty-two in number? 2, 3. Those who believe are worthy to be called Israelites—that is, “seeing God,” 80, 84.

## J

**JACOB** was a figure of the people of the nations, while Esau was a figure of the Hebrews, 523. The interpretations of the twelve names of Jacob’s sons, and how they signify the stages by which one proceeds from the conversion of sinners to God, 534.

**JAMES** was called the brother of the Lord because Joseph, his father, was also called the Lord’s father, 213.

**JANUS** was a human being and the founder of a single city, which is now called Janiculum, 400.

Those who celebrated the **KALENDS OF JANUARY** are rebuked, 399.

**JEABARIM** signifies “a heap of stones of those crossing over,” 18.

The condition of **FASTING** imposes upon us the condition of endurance, 419. Fasting is the contrition and humiliation of the soul, 333. Those who fast from food but do not abstain from evil are like the devil, who does not eat and nevertheless does not cease from evil, 431. Our fasts ought not to be occupied with the activities of the world, but exercised in the sacred writings, 429. What you withhold from yourselves by fasting you ought to send on to heaven for the poor, 431—and you ought to give it all to the poor, 426. What power and grace does fasting possess? 418. It brought Moses near to participation in divinity, 414. Fasts are the Christian’s camp, 418. Faith and fasting are the swift feet of the soul, 415. How poorly some people excuse themselves from fasting! 443. A person fasts long enough when he refreshes himself in accordance with Christ’s will, 422. See **ABSTINENCE, LENT**.

**JEPHTHAH** was found faithful when he offered his daughter according to the vow he had foolishly made, 164.

**JEREMIAH** is the most widely accepted of the prophets, 353.

**JERICHO** signifies the whole body of the reprobate, which is the city of the devil, 503.

**JETHERBATHA** is interpreted as “goodness,” 15.

**JOHN THE BAPTIST** was conceived by Elizabeth not by nature but by grace, 459. The naming of him restored a voice to the mute, piety to the father, and a priest to the people, 461. The births of Christ and John are compared with one another, 459. In what sense is everyone born of a woman inferior to John? 461. His birthday is celebrated, 459. How is he the voice of one crying out? 461. He was fasting, humble, frugal, and a virgin, 462. It is no wonder that, shut up in prison, he continually proclaimed Christ to his disciples, since, even while shut up in the womb, he proclaimed the same Lord through his movements, 460. When his head was cut off, it was a type of the Law, 462. See **CHRIST**.

**JOHN THE EVANGELIST** was the first to recognize the Lord, because it was fitting that virginity should first recognize a virginal body, 340. He wrote only what he foresaw would be especially beneficial to posterity, 499. Why was he compelled to write the Gospel after his return from exile? 542. The holy Fathers transmit that after his return he preached only at Ephesus and in the surrounding regions, and that he died there, 543. He died without being killed by the sword, 503.

**JOB** was one of Esau’s sons, the fifth from Abraham—that is, Esau’s grandson, 81.

**JOSEPH**, the betrothed of Mary, had sons from another wife, 213.

**JOSEPHUS** is cited, 5, 16, 19, 560. He describes the overthrow of Jerusalem, 503.

The surname **JEW** is understood to have a threefold meaning, 40. They began to be called Jews from the time of Judas Maccabaeus, 31. Their prerogatives, 42. Why does Paul place the Jew before others? 38. The Jews must be regarded as apostates: because they do not receive Christ, they are guilty of violating the Law, 84. Jews lived in Rome in the time of the apostles, 25. Those among them who had believed handed down to the Romans that those professing Christ should keep the Law, ibid. They did not believe rightly concerning Christ, ibid. If some killed the Lord and persecuted his apostles, by the time the vision of the Apocalypse was shown to John they had already been devastated by the Romans, 564. How severe God is toward them! 92. The Jews’ conversation among themselves is a great pollution, 400. Their faithlessness will be indicated by the faith of the apostles, 39. Their rejection made room for the nations, 91, 93. The calling of the nations is the destruction of the Jews, 523. Their case is nearly more serious in their own eyes than that of the nations, 38. It is established that at the end of the world they will return to the faith of Christ through the preaching of Elijah and Enoch, 543, 545.

**JUDAS MACCABAEUS** was one of the sons of Aaron, 31.

When **JUDAS** was a thief, the Lord did not reject him merely because he had not been accused, 127.

The **DAY OF JUDGMENT** will not come until the number of the elect has been fulfilled, 533. On it the sign of the Son of Man—that is, Christ’s cross—will appear, 422. In what form will Christ then be seen by the wicked and by the just? 500. The Lord will not come before the Roman kingdom has fallen and the Antichrist appears, who will kill the saints after restoring freedom to the Romans, though under his own name, 286.

It is not proper for a **JUDGE** to condemn without an accuser, 127. In judgment never abandon mercy, 489.

The **JURISTS**, or pontiffs—whom they call priests—established certain days on which judgment was given, 124.

**JUSTICE** is recognized with nature itself as guide, 93. The first justice is to acknowledge the Creator, and then to keep what he has commanded, 85. Justice should be regarded as common, 97. True justice is to give from one’s own possessions to the person who has none, 164. Its way must be followed so that one may rightly arrive at mercy, 281. Perfect justice is goodness, 53. It is impious justice not to forgive human frailty, 489. How does the justice of Christians abound and appear to surpass the ordinary measure? 97. The Spirit is given for justification, so that he may justify through his assistance, 72. Justification is fulfilled in us when remission of all sins is granted, 71. The just are called stones, 18. They are rightly called inhabitants of heaven, 537. What is the redemption of the just? 556.

**YOUTH** is generally more ready to fall, 315.

## L
LABOR: He labors in the hope that fruit may be obtained, 141. Natural reason dictates that one should live from the place where one labors, 141. No one hates his own labor, 235. Whoever glories in his labor does not glory beyond measure, 197. Those who devote themselves to labor turn away from evil thoughts, 278. It is fitting for one who labors that the Lord’s glory should appear, so that by seeing the reward he may endure his labors more eagerly, 8. What is labor in the Lord? 109.

TEARS: their office is blessed, 603. [Col. 1239]

LATINS: Latins commonly sing in Greek, delighted by the sound of the words, although they do not know what they are saying, 157.

THIEF: On the cross he immediately obtained baptism through the shedding of blood, and, reddened with blood as a confessor, entered paradise with the Lord, 596.

PRAISE: Whoever sees himself praised deliberately labors to make true the things that are said, 106. So too does the one who sees that people think well of him, 192, 318. Some are accustomed to feel shame and correct themselves when they hear good things said about them, 130.

LAURENCE: consumed on a gridiron, 458. The coals were a place of refreshment for him, 6.

LEBNA: the same as “whitening,” 12.

READERS: how can they be called shepherds? 241.

AMBASSADORS: The law concerning human ambassadors is not to inflict destruction, 250. No one sends an outstanding and very great gift through an unworthy person, 237.

LEVITES: Why were they commanded to shave all the hair of their flesh? 10. The Law is threefold, 45. The Law is fourfold, 68. The Law is the judge of sin, not its mother; it makes sinners guilty, 64. The form of each law ought to be seen in the profession and conduct of its worshiper, 150. Whoever naturally observes justice is a guardian of the Law, 38. Knowledge of the Law strengthens minds and urges them toward progress in a better hope, 156. Greater knowledge of the Law makes one more guilty, 144. The Law rules over those who err, 228. The Law leads the sinner to death, but benefits the obedient unto life, 65. Repeated instruction in the Law makes the negligent more attentive, 212. Those who have been justified are friends of the Law, 71. Whoever hears that the one from whom he received the Law is coming will be more anxious lest he be ashamed when that one arrives, 168.

The natural law has three parts; what are they? 55. No one endowed with reason is permitted to be ignorant of it, 502, 568. Is it fitting that a person who knows the Creator should restrain his life without the Law, and why? 55. The Law of God must be observed with every possible and the greatest diligence, 15. He is ungrateful for God’s mercy who wishes to remain under the Law, 26. The Law of Moses is not evil, 64. Why is it called old? ibid. Why was it given in written form? 93. Formerly the Gentiles were subject to it, 38. How was sin not imputed until the Law? 53. How was it given so that sin might abound? 58. There was bitter water at Marah, 416. It is called spiritual, 66, though not life-giving, 69. It is the spirit of fear, 73. Through sacrifices and certain legal observances some sins of the ancient people were removed, 515. If you attend only to the letter, the legal commandments will seem useless to you; but if you understand their spiritual meaning, great truth shines forth for you, 530. The Law brings no one who understands it carnally to perfection, but raises the one who understands it spiritually to the summit of perfection, 529. Its teaching is threefold, 40. All salvation in it concerns Christ, 41. What is the righteousness of the Law? 85. Its righteousness is Christian faith, 41. Whoever believes in Christ possesses its perfection, 86. He fulfills the Law who comes through the Law of Moses to Christ, 85. He does not fulfill it who does not believe in Christ, 38, 40, 41. He does not abolish it who now teaches that it ought to cease, 47. From the time of Christ, the indulgence promised in the Law has been granted, 85. The difference between Christ’s law and Judaism, 214. The new Law is written in the mind, that is, in the heart—not by a pen, but by the Spirit, 176. What is the law of the spirit? 64. What is the difference when one says “spiritual law” and “law of the spirit”? 70. The laws of the Romans were brought from Athens, just as those of the Greeks came from the Hebrews, 62.

BOOK OF LIFE: the predestination of almighty God, 551.

To be free from God is the greatest crime, 135. One becomes free by receiving remission of sins, 225. What is willingly heard is easily done, 488.

BOOKS: In ancient times they were made from papyrus, 525.

LAWFUL: Is everything that is not lawful prohibited? 130.

LYNX: According to the tales, it could see through a wall, 340.

TONGUE: restraint, 17. Not everything should be said to everyone, 279. It is superfluous to say what is already known, 277. The kind of speech reveals the kind of mind, 488. It may seem unbelievable that one who speaks badly lives well, 244.

LOMBARDS: They claimed Italy for themselves, 564.

LUKE: He is held to have written the Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles, 276.

MOURNING: the weeping of many days, 575.

MOON: It is said to be in the third circle, 204.

LUST: What vices does it generate? 495. The Fathers often used *luxuria* for sexual desire, 549.

M

MACELOTH: interpreted as “from the beginning,” 13.

MACCABEES: martyrs, 469.

AUTHORITY OF OFFICE: Authority appropriate to the office is then granted if it rests upon one’s own example, 594. It is the mark of a suitable teacher that he fulfills in his deeds what he teaches in words, 288. Whatever is done wrong by pupils reflects upon teachers, 566. Whoever despises his teacher seeks to be corrected, 207. See DISCIPLE.

MAGOG: interpreted as “from the roof,” 572.

MAIANUS AND VITALINUS: They are praised because they contributed all their property toward the building of the church, 477.

WICKEDNESS: It acts against itself, 98, 253. When the seed of wickedness is removed, the fruit of evil will wither, 35. There is one cause of all evils: evil, 45. The evil hidden within is extinguished more quickly, 494. Repentance binds the one who does evil and the one who consents to it with equal force, 489. Who is inexperienced in evil? 110. Everyone knows his own evils better than another’s, 130. Whoever rejoices in another’s evils is easily deceived, 91. It is better to hate evils than to share in them, 488. Why is the table of the wicked accursed? 90.

MANASSES: The repentance of King Manasses is set forth as an example, 598.

SLAVES: Why are they so called? 274.

COMMANDMENTS OF GOD: Contempt for them is a cruel and most grievous wound, 559.

MANICHAEANS: their errors, 112, 296. They deny that Christ was human, 251, though they do not deny that he was crucified, 210. They possess various strange speculations, called by inflated names, 311. Diocletian identified them in his constitution, 310. Their deceptions, ibid.

MANNA: It can signify wisdom, which is Christ, 506.

DWELLINGS OF THE ISRAELITES: Christ comes to heaven, Israel to the Jordan, and the Christian to heaven by an equal number of stages, 3. See ISRAELITES.

HAND: Your hand can be healthy if it is withdrawn from evils but extended toward good works, 412.

MARANATHA: It means “the Lord comes,” 170.

MARAH: a place in the desert of Shur, so called because of the bitterness of its waters, 6.

MARCION: his error, 112, 125. From whom did he derive it? 117. He appears, through hatred of the Law, to deny Christ and his body while professing Jesus, 26. Marcion the monster, 453. The Marcionites have almost disappeared, 296.

MARY: a virgin before childbirth, a virgin in childbirth, and a virgin after childbirth, 546. She was a shining, slender rod—and a virgin—who, through the integrity of her body, brought forth Christ like a flower, 430. It is an impious assertion to say that the Lord’s true brothers were born of Mary, 214. Mary is both mother and daughter of the Church, 547. Comparison of Eve and Mary, 450. The Ark of the Covenant is a figure of Mary, 447. How aptly may she be compared with a fleece? 397. She is represented by the eastern gate, 579. See CHRIST.

In MARTHA, Christ heals a prolonged flow of blood, 454.

MARTYRDOM: Its glory is acquired through sufferings and afflictions, 49. The mother of martyrdom is Catholic faith, 466. From one grain of Christ’s body, how great a harvest of martyrs sprang forth? 473. Christ is slain in them, 180. A tyrant could never have benefited them so much by favor as he benefited them by hatred, 467. The martyr’s victory is the judgment of the persecutor, 473. The martyr’s palm is a kind of reward, 416. Martyrs teach by the power of their deeds and persuade through the suffering of martyrdom, 473. Let us honor the blessed martyrs, leaders of the faith, intercessors for the world, heralds of the kingdom, 467. Why should their bodies be honored? ibid. Whoever honors them also honors Christ, 465. God wishes the merits of the martyrs to be our support, and their sufferings to be our progress, 466.

MARRIAGE: A marriage is not valid if it is without devotion to God, 134. Consequently, it is not a sin for one who is dismissed for God’s sake to join himself to another, ibid. A man may take a wife if he has dismissed a sinful wife; the reverse is not permitted to a wife, 133. Husbands too are censured for the insolence of women, 159. God’s cause is greater than that of marriage, 134. No one should join himself to his wife before the octave of Easter, 425. See UNION, NUPTIALS.

MEDIATOR: that is, arbitrator, 221.

PHYSICIANS: Ancient physicians, in the case of persons worthy of death or already condemned to death, investigated how they might benefit the living by opening up what lay hidden in the human being, 83. It is the physician’s praise if he cures many, 233. What physician would not rebuke a patient for treating himself carelessly? 171.

MEDITATION: Daily meditation removes sleepiness and produces watchfulness, 96.

BETTER THINGS: One must always proceed toward better things, 16.

LIMBS: All the limbs suffer together with the grief of one, 173. It contributes to the usefulness and rest of the limbs if the head is not disturbed, 31.

MEMORY: Whoever always remembers someone is written in that person’s mind, 176.

LIE: It is established not only in false words but also in feigned deeds, 432. Every sin can be understood as a lie, 584. Various kinds of lies are described, 576. The lies of certain monks, so that they might be regarded as great by people, 577. Why is every human being a liar? 42. How so? 432.

MIND: The good mind is superior to the other portions of human substance, 4. The mind is like the head of a household, 509. See SOUL. [Col. 1241]

MONTHS: The moon produces their course; the sun produces the day, 224.

MERIT: God rewards or condemns each person according to his own merit, 38.

METCHA: In Latin it is called “new death,” 13.

MICHAEL: His name means “Who is like God”; he signifies Christ, 547.

MILLENARIANS: Some fell into heresy by saying that after the resurrection Christ would reign bodily with all the saints for a thousand years, 587. The resurrection will take place after the thousand years during which the Savior will reign here, once Antichrist has been destroyed, 166.

MIRACLES: Why do they not now occur as they did at the beginning of the Church? 154.

MERCY: When mercy is presumed upon, the severity of justice is softened, 595. Mercy is manifold, 95. It ought to be practiced simply and joyfully, 96. Everyone who believes in God ought to devote himself to mercy, 316. Its recompense or reward is that those who receive mercy should show mercy, 107. Mercy cannot be attributed to anyone unless he possesses justice, 98. In mercy there is full and perfect justice, 246. See ALMSGIVING.

MASS: Throughout nearly all the Eastern churches and some Western ones, during the offering of sacrifices the people sing the *trisagion* with the priest: “Holy, holy, etc.,” 608. Prayers preparing for Mass, 489 and following. By whom should Mass be heard daily? 425.

MOAB: the name of a city and province, 7.

MODESTY: How much does it advance one? 309. It produces progress, 240. It must be maintained in the Church, 423.

MONK: A monk who follows a young woman laughing immoderately is censured, 463. We have seen some leave monasteries, give themselves over to the service of powerful persons, and return to monasteries, 539. The vices of certain persons living in monasteries are scourged, 517. See LIE.

MONTANUS: Montanus, Priscilla, and Maximilla were prophets of the Cataphrygians, 284. The caves of Montanus resound with the two prophetesses, Priscilla and Maximilla, like the dogs of Scylla, 453.

CUSTOMS: How can good customs be wings for us? 419.

DEATH: It is threefold: natural, penal, and spiritual, 14. The first and second deaths, 51, 54, 572. What is true death? 464. The profit of sin is death, 62. It produces gain when one sins, 64. We have seen some who sought death and did not find it, 538. What is the kingdom of death? 56. Death inflicted by the faithless is life among believers, 208.

MORTIFICATION: To chastise the body is to afflict it with fasts and give it what benefits life, not luxury, 143.

MOSEROTH: interpreted as “disciplines,” 14.

MOSES: His principal deeds and certain commandments are explained mystically, 525, 526 and following. Moses was, as it were, the brighter right hand of the Jewish people, 411. The Holy Spirit wrote the tablets of Moses, 607. The end of Moses, 20. It is a fable of certain Jews that his burial was hidden lest he be raised by magicians, 316. The glory of Moses is abolished when the glory of Christ appears, 177.

WOMEN: They are veiled so that they may appear humbled, 159. How should they stand before a bishop? 148. How unbecoming is the proud adornment of women? 293. Among Roman women the use of wine was once unknown, as the use of water is now, 273. See FEMALE.

WORLD: It is twofold, 129. It was created in spring, 437. Its four roots are enumerated, 2. “The world,” that is, human beings, 91, 115. It is called unbelief, and why? 125. For Christians this world is a sea, and why? 175. What is the spirit of the world? 119. Why are all things in the world vain? 74. Love of the age joins its lovers to the earth so that they become one with it, 567. It is difficult to love God and the world at the same time, 490. Like one buried, have no concern for this age, ibid. The faithful use the things of the world only to relieve the needs of the body, 525. When concern for the age is diminished, one watches more attentively over the things of God, 137. Whoever does not do the things of the world or of error is dead to the world, 218. The righteous do not fear leaving this age but rejoice, and why? 181. We who have abandoned the conduct of the age ought to seek a pure and heavenly life, 10.

GIFTS: They blind the eyes and weaken the force of authority, 190.

TO MURMUR: to complain falsely to one another about superiors and rulers, 144.

CHANGEABLE: A thing subject to time and age is always changeable, 53.

MYSTERY OF INIQUITY: It began with Nero and continued through Diocletian and, most recently, Julian, 286.

N

NARCISSUS: A presbyter who performed the office of a foreigner, 109.

NATURE: No one can change nature except the one who is Lord of nature, 401. [Col. 1242]

NAZIRITES: The life of those who abstain and practice continence is signified by the name Nazirites, 9.

NAZARIUS: The Church of Milan preserves the martyr Nazarius whole in body, 466. The universal Church celebrates his birthday with festive rejoicing, ibid. His martyrdom is described, ibid.

NEGLIGENTLY: If anything is done negligently and without devotion, it incurs blame, 257.

NEW MOONS: They are lunar days, 223. They are called the beginnings of months, 270.

NEOPHYTE: What is a neophyte? 361.

NERO: See MYSTERY.

NICENE COUNCIL: We know that its decree was set against all heresies with unconquerable truth, 358.

NICOLAUS: A heretic in the time of the apostles, 537. The Nicolaitans were heretics, 505. They detested marriage, 506.

NOAH: He was the first person pronounced righteous in the Old Scripture and the tenth from the protoplast, 2.

NAMES: Among our ancestors they were formed according to reason, 26. An appellative name exists only in the word, not in the nobility of nature, 256.

NOVATIAN: 11. He was a man of no small learning, but, turning toward schism, created a heresy, 155. He is censured for saying that he possessed the Church among his own people and all the purified, 309. He says that fornicators cannot complete repentance and be received into communion; but this contradicts the Apostle’s judgment, 207. In Novatian’s view, the fornicator seems to sin against the body of Christ or against the Holy Spirit because of the cause for which he was cut off from the Church, 131. The Novatians, 39, 113, 114. They reject those baptized by us, ibid.

BOOK OF NUMBERS: Why is one of the five books of Moses so called? 1.

NUMBER: The number two is mystical, 3. Four is perfect, 2, as is six, 410, 573. Six signifies the perfection of the saints, 516. Seven and eight, 504. Ten is mystical and perfect, 2. The mysteries of the twenty-four numbers are explained, 516.

MESSENGER: No one announces a trivial matter through great forerunners, 27.

NUPTIALS: First marriages are solemnly celebrated under God’s blessing; second marriages are permitted but lack the former glory, 138. What does it mean to marry in the Lord? 138. Unwilling marriages commonly have bad outcomes, 138. See MARRIAGE.

O

OBEDIENCE: No one obeys another better than one who serves out of charity, 232. Voluntary service is usually more acceptable than forced service, 444. Service is to be rendered to each person according to his rank and merits, 183.

OFFERINGS: The offerings of the first Christians, 149. An offering should be made every week; and, even if not daily for strangers, at least twice a week for residents, 295. Whatever is offered with complete faith and a sober mind is purified by the Holy Spirit, 106.

OBOTH: It is interpreted as “among magicians,” 18.

EIGHTH DAY: The resurrection is understood by it, 7.

EYES: Their history is always examined, 473.

Ὁμοιούσιον: The Greeks call it “another identical thing with one,” 354. How can this word be said to be found in the Scriptures? 352. Those are censured who, after removing ὁμοιούσιον—that is, the term “of one substance”—put ὁμοούσιον, that is, “similar to the maker,” in its place, 348. Their objection—that the word ὁμοούσιον is not found in the Scriptures—is answered, 349.

ONESIMUS: The Apostle baptized him while he was in custody in the city of Rome, 318.

WORKS: By his works each person will either be justified or condemned, 99, and will receive his reward, 186. We carry with us nothing except good or evil works, 342. It is no small offense to confess God as Lord while serving the devil by one’s actions, 61. The perfection of the saints grows through good works, 529. God regenerated us through faith in Christ so that, trained in good works, we might be worthy to receive the promises, 235. Fear of the Lord drives one to repentance, and repentance urges one to do good works, 555. Deeds persuade more than words, 288. See ACTS, FAITH.

PRAYER: Various kinds of prayer are reported, 535. Prayer is exceedingly necessary, 96. To pray in the spirit is to direct prayer to God with a clean conscience and complete faith, 250. One must cry out to the Lord not so much with the mouth as with the heart, 445. It is not a place that commends prayer, but a devout mind, 29. The mind should be peaceful in prayer, 293. How can we pray without ceasing? 517. The confirmation of prayer is completed through those who respond “Amen,” 157. It is impossible that the prayers of many should not obtain something, 108. Many easily obtain what they desire, 284. According to what ecclesiastical rule should our priests pray for everyone? 292. We are aided by the prayers of approved and holy men, 364. Wonderful is the power of prayer, 9. The intention of God when he threatens is tempered by the modesty of the most humble prayer, 593. The weakness of prayer, 76. Assiduous prayers move the mind of the judge to show mercy, 283.

ORDER: It is proper that we proceed from small things to great, 6.

ORDINATION: What does it mean that the grace of the ordainer is given through prophecy and the laying on of hands? 298.

ORIGEN: He was called a pillar of the Church, but because of his erroneous teaching he departed from it, 510.

OS EROTH: In another translation, Phiairoth; it is interpreted as “mouth of nobles.” It is a village and suburb of Magdali, 5.

KISS: What is the holy kiss? 109. It is a sign of peace, 170.

P

PEACEFUL: The one who harms no one appears peaceful, 98. Every good life is tranquil, and modest actions are peaceful; by these one goes to God, 44. Whoever is at peace with God fears no one’s hostility, 231.

PAGANS: While celebrating their mysteries in darkness in a cave, they are deceived with covered eyes, 246.

PALMS OR OLIVES: The festival, 433. It is celebrated five days before the Passion, 434.

PARABLES: If you attend to the words of the parables, you will see that they are lies; but if you consider their meaning, you will recognize the truth, 530.

PARADISE: It signifies the Church, 505, 520.

PASSOVER: It is a sacrifice, not a passage, as some think, 128. Passover is called a passage, 436, and also the Passion of the Savior, 437. How should the feast of Passover be celebrated? ibid. Baptism is celebrated at it, 438. A psalm is customarily sung at it, ibid. The Passion is life for Christians, and persecution is defense, 312. Sufferings reveal merit for the future life, 180.

SHEPHERDS: At the birth of the Son of God, they signified preachers, 394. See CHRIST.

TO SUFFER: To suffer unjustly, while being able to resist but unwilling to do so, is the glory of the one who suffers, 116. Whoever suffers for God’s justice is sacrificed to God, 311. It is great grief if someone suffers for those among whom he accomplishes nothing, 257. Afflictions are examples of future merits in those who suffer for glory, 285.

PATIENCE: It saves human beings, 185. Its sweetest good is that in which the salvation of our souls is especially placed, 494.

FATHERS: Ambrose, Hilary, Jerome, Augustine, Gregory, and many others published a very large number of books by which the heresies that existed or could exist were destroyed, 550. Jerome, Augustine, Gregory, 583.

PATRIARCHS: Learn obedience from Abraham, chastity from Joseph, and humility from David, 434.

PATRICIANISTS: their errors, 296.

FATHER: The Father’s light is inaccessible, because no one has ever seen him, 304. Why is the Father alone called immortal and invisible? 291. It is characteristic of a father to show his children an affectionate kindness, offering indulgence according to the diversity of their conduct, 407. The dignity begun by the father is ennobled in his sons, 40.

PAULINUS: A judge who persecutes Christians, 485.

PAUL: Why was he first called Saul and then Paul? 26. In baptism he changed both his conduct and his name, 421. God struck him and thereby made him healthy, 413. Why was he called the vessel of election by divine judgment? 119. He is understood to have been carried beyond all the stars of the world, 204, first as far as the third heaven and then into the heavenly paradise, ibid. As a Pharisee, he held the office of teacher in Judaism, 26. He did nothing without the Spirit of God, 174. From morning until the fifth hour he sought his livelihood with his hands, and from then until the tenth hour he debated publicly, 202. He also taught at night, 203. Why did he devote himself to human labor? 278. Why did he refuse expenses offered to him? 142, 299. Because he placed charity before everything, he followed what would benefit the brethren, 254. He was a divine man and a spiritual physician, 120. Traveling in winter, when rains are frequent, he encountered danger from overflowing rivers as he went out, 202. For this reason he believed that he was helped more by God because he had been abandoned by human beings, 312. Paul came to Peter not to learn anything from him but because of the affection of the apostolate, 213. He could learn nothing from the other apostles, 214, 216. He did not pretend, 142. He accommodated himself to the time, 96. See PETER.

He remained among the Corinthians for one year and six months, 111. The varying order of Paul’s letters, 313. Repetition in the letter was not superfluous, 110. Paul writes to the Romans in four ways, 25. For what reasons did he write to the Corinthians? 111. Before this letter he had written another to the same people, ibid., 128. Why did he write the second letter to the Corinthians? 169. He wrote to the Ephesians concerning the custody of the city of Rome, 231. Why did he write to the Colossians? 263. And to the Thessalonians? 275, [Col. 1244] 276. And to Timothy? 303. And why did he write to Philemon? 317.

POVERTY: It is plainly rich in itself: it spends everything and possesses everything, 478.

PEACE: One peace belongs to God, another to the world, 209. God’s very nature is peace, 261. Without Christ there is neither peace nor hope, 28. The peace of Christ is not a matter of debt but of merit, 396. Whoever has peace with God does not fear every hostile mind, 261. Peace is the gateway of love, 251. Those who are called to peace ought to devote themselves to patience, 159.

SIN: There are three kinds of sin, 48. Adam first sold himself, and consequently all his offspring is subject to sin, 66. It is clear that all sinned in Adam as in a mass, 54. The curse of the first man passed to all human beings, 586. A human being is born under sin, 68. Knowledge of evil descends from original sin, 586. Adam, by sinning, found death, and held all his descendants through his origin, 162, 166. He left it to us by right of inheritance, 73. Christ was not subject to original sin, because he was not born from the intercourse of a man, which cannot be without sin, 530. If original sin had not existed, there would be no vice, 527. Through transmission all flesh becomes flesh of sin, 68. Every sin is flesh, 73. How does sin dwell in the flesh when it is not a substance? 67, 68. When the body is contaminated, no one doubts that the sin belongs to the soul, 34. When the soul’s thought is criminal, bodies are said to be defiled, 34. Certain light sins, through their accumulation, become more serious than some that are considered grave, 578. Apart from other sins, it appears that there is another sin called sin against the Holy Spirit, 132. There is a certain measure of offenses; when sinners have filled it, they are judged entirely unworthy of life, 66. Every sin fears being made public, 246. Those who obey sin are called mortal, 60. Sin rules over those who sin, 61. Since sins cannot cease to exist, at least let them not reign, 603. One subject to sin does what he does not wish, 67. Yet for that reason he is not free from guilt, ibid. What does it mean to be sold under sin? 66. The day of wrath is for sinners, 37. Remove sins from your midst, and you have made God near to you, 420. Whoever afflicts himself as the cause of his own offense takes vengeance upon himself, 189. The Apostle was so disposed that he grieved over the faults of others as though they were his own, 30. The person whose offense causes many to suffer becomes more guilty, 174. The one whose sin has harmed others should be reproached, 93. Sin was condemned by the Savior in three ways, 71. To remit, cover, and not impute sin are one method and one meaning, 48. To forgive sins and give the Spirit belongs to God alone, 121. No sinner’s purity can be perfected without the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit, 528. To grant pardon to sinners is nothing other than grace, 89. How much better is God at healing the sins of the soul than a physician at healing the body? 591. The remission of sins removes all sins, 69. What is so welcome and pleasant as to preach indulgence to sinners? 291. Death is the end of sin, 59.

MOST DECEITFUL: 601.

TREACHERY: It stains everything, 234. One must behave prudently among the treacherous, 247.

PERSECUTION: The dignity of the one whose bonds in Christ are made manifest grows as they multiply, 252.

PERSONS: They do not divide the substance, 248.

PETER: The Apostle Peter is called from the Rock, Christ, just as a Christian is called from Christ, 449. Cephas himself is Simon Peter, first among the apostles, 140. He is first among the apostles, and how much more so among the others? 198. Andrew did not receive the primacy, but Peter did, 205. He was first among the apostles, to whom the Savior entrusted care of the churches, 213. Why did Christ choose Peter’s boat? 439. How is Peter the foundation of the Church? 580. By walking on the sea he taught that it was not the body but faith that walked, 340. There is tranquility when Peter alone sails; there is a storm when Judas is added, 440. Why did he become hungry after prayer? 464. What is Peter’s key? 435. Peter and Paul were teachers of the nations, authors of the martyrs, and leaders of the priests, 465. What was the reason for which Peter was rebuked by Paul? 217. Who would dare resist Peter, the first apostle, unless it were another who knew, through confidence in his own election, that he was not inferior? 217. Full authority was evidently given to Peter in preaching Judaism, while Paul’s perfect authority is found in preaching to the nations, 216. The birthday of the apostles Peter and Paul is celebrated, 463.

PHARAOH: The name was used for kings among the Egyptians, 82.

PHARISEE: See PAUL. The men sent to explore the Promised Land presented an image of scribes and Pharisees, 11.

PHILEMON: a praiseworthy man, one of the common people, 317.

PHILIP: He buried the bodies of Saints Gervasius and Protasius, 486.

PHILOSOPHERS: The teaching of philosophers and poets was full of every kind of lie and error, 563. How aptly may the teaching of philosophers be compared with serpents? 541. How foolishly do the wise men of the world say that what God has done is foolish because he has done more than human beings understand? 71.

PHINON: interpreted as “restraint of the mouth,” 17.

PHOENIX: How does it rise again from its own ashes? 342.

PHOTINUS: his error, 125. He denies that Christ is God, 26, 210, 218, 251. Its authors, 41. The Charybdis of Photinianism, 453. The Photinians, 113.

PHRYGIA: Unless an impure person is present, the sacrament is mute and religion grows numb, 62.

IDLE: In divine conduct, the idle person is without hope, 96.

TO FATTEN: to make the soul fat, 601.

PLEBS: There is diversity in every people, 258.

RAIN: From where does it arise? 572.

REPENTANCE: It is to mourn past evils and not commit again the things that must be mourned, 425. It is the condemnation of the former age and the promised correction in the future, 589. This is true repentance: to cease from sin now, 174. Repentance has no excuse, but confession, 189. To acknowledge one’s guilt is the beginning of confession, and what remorse urges becomes the nearest approach to pardon, 595. The more heavily you are burdened with the load of sins, the more insistently you must perform the duty of confession, so that what you are not worthy to demand through friendship you may obtain through shameless persistence, 595. Repentance must now be practiced, 423. The confession and repentance of the Ninevites are set before the repentant and described [reading uncertain] in detail, 593. David’s twofold repentance, 594. The repentance of the tax collector is set forth as an example, 598, as is that of the sinful woman, ibid., and of the prodigal son, 599. See AHAB, MANASSES.

The Lord delays punishment in order to find repentance; he prolongs patience lest mercy lose what ought to have been accomplished by discipline, 601. Grave sins reach pardon only through weeping and groaning, 93. Whoever wishes to exact punishment for graver sins with unsuitable vengeance weakens the person whom he could have had corrected and healthy, 98. The filth of the body is an adornment of repentance, 593. The discipline of repentance is harsh, but becomes gentler if the measure of the fault is considered, 599. Repentance produces great agitation and disturbance, 3. There Ahab, the king of Nineveh, and the Corinthians established their dwelling, 4. If repentance comes from a true heart, it immediately bears fruit, 174. The one who is permitted to repent possesses the sure gift of pardon, 604. Through mercy God regenerates and reforms penitents again, so that there may be not merely pardon but restoration to their former condition, 170. Repentance is like an eye-salve, 511. A person placed in the punishment of the future life will repent without benefit from repentance, 37. Who is a repentant person? 427. What ought he to do? 5. He is anxious lest he sin again, 189. He is safe if he does not doubt the remission granted by indulgence, 594.

COMMANDMENTS: Those of the New Testament are more severe than those of the Old, 508.

PREDESTINATION: Whom does God predestine? 76, 77, 81. A person is chosen for a time not from foreknowledge but on account of present righteousness, 76. To prepare someone for glory or destruction means to know beforehand what will happen, 84. Can someone be erased from the book of predestination? 509. See GOD, BOOK.

PREACHING: The priest’s preaching to the people for their salvation is correction and the testimony of the one who judges, 448. It does not need pomp or ornament of speech, 114. Whoever wishes to adorn Christ’s faith with his words seeks his own glory, ibid. In religion, force of speech is necessary, not sweet speech, 199. In the Church, the person who speaks ought to be the one who benefits everyone, 156. Whoever preaches without being sent is presumptuous and rejected, 197. It is a sign of a devout and faithful preacher if he does not fear speaking the word of God in affliction, 278. Whoever acts differently from what he preaches makes his hearers suspicious, so that they doubt the promises, 143. When someone’s life is despised, his preaching too must be held in contempt, 544. The glory of preachers is when their hearers readily believe, 279. Preachers carried Christ in heart and tongue, 503. The two silver trumpets signified preachers, 10. They are designated by the stars, ibid.

PRESBYTERS: They are vicars of Christ, 301. One should not readily believe a charge against a presbyter, and why? 300. In Egypt, presbyters confirm when the bishop is absent, 241. See BISHOP.

FIRSTFRUITS: They are to be offered in the Church, 243.

PRISCILLA: 30.

PRIVILEGE: Whoever enjoys another’s privilege will be deprived of his own merit, 594.

PROFESSION: Nothing is more dangerous than for deeds to contradict one’s profession, 300. The praise and power of God are found no more in profession than in deeds, 310.

PROPHET: It is impossible for a prophet to be deceived, 314. Prophets speak of the future and reveal the Scriptures, 153, 156. Prophets are interpreters of the Scriptures, 241. To prophesy is to declare by a symbolic voice, after prayer, that the Lord’s coming will take place, 147. Prophecy is the first proof that our faith is rational, 95.

SUCCESSFULLY: Whatever is done simply in devotion to God can turn out well, 224. [Col. 1246]

PROTASIUS: See GERVASIUS.

NEIGHBOR: It is a great glory, if you were able to harm someone, to spare him and not repay the one who sins against you according to his guilt, 488. Know that as much can be forgiven you as you yourself have forgiven your debtor, 602. See CHARITY.

PRUDENCE: It consists in benefiting some more than harming others, 95. It is the mark of a prudent person to know how to answer each individual, 247. The ancients defined all prudent people as free, but all foolish people as slaves, 275. It is difficult to be prudent in great matters yet unwise in small ones, 33. The prudent do not wish to put themselves forward, 201. What is the prudence of the flesh, and why is it so called? 71. The prudence of the world is hostile to religion, 117.

PRUDENTIUS: He discussed excellently in verse the conflict between vices and virtues, 549.

PSALMIST: 88, 104, 141, 359, 453, 484, 587.

PSEUDO-APOSTLES: They preached the name of Christ with philosophy mixed in, 112.

SHAME: Shame accomplishes nothing when justice is neglected, 94.

BEAUTY: God commonly judges beautiful what appears contemptible to human beings, 153.

PURGATORIAL FIRE: 553, 572, 580. Who, purified through fire, will be saved so as not to be tormented forever in eternal fire like the treacherous? 122.

PURPLE: It is a royal ornament, 583.

PYTHON: What do they call a python? 119.

Q
## QUADRAGESIMA

Lent is a time of redemption and, in a certain sense, of heavenly medicine, 413. What should be done during it, 414, 422, 424. It was not established by human beings but consecrated by divine authority, 429. It is shown to be mystical and most sacred, 421. Its observances are called “stations,” 418. They must be guarded with every observance, 419. Why does it contain forty-two days? 415. They are compared with the encampments of the Israelites, 415, 416, 417. Various ways of keeping Lent, 410. Those who dine for seven days and fast for seven days are censured, 421. It is no slight sin to violate the prescribed Lent, 418, 420. Whoever violates it for one day is judged a violator of the whole of Lent, 429. It is good to fast at all times, but better to fast during Lent with Christ, 420, 421. No one should eat or drink before the ninth hour during it, 425.

## QUINQUAGESIMA

The Sunday of Quinquagesima, 409. Why is it so called? 410. Instituted by Pope Telesphorus, ibid. Some falsely claim that they observe a quinquagesima, 420.

# R

## RAHAB

She prefigured the Church, 454.

## RAMESSES

An Egyptian city; its name is interpreted as “turbulent commotion” and signifies repentance, 3. The first encampment of the Israelites, and what happened there, 4.

## RAPHIDIM

Its name is interpreted as “praise of judgment,” 9. The eleventh encampment of the Israelites, adorned with the distinction of three marvelous works, 8.

## REDEEMS

No one redeems anything unless it had been his own, 117.

## KINGS

They bear the image of God, 99. Affliction arises from the discord of kings, 394.

## RELIGION

Not to know the faith of one’s religion and profession is to be reprobate, 208.

## REMITTED

To receive what has been remitted, 269.

## REMONPHARES

Its name is interpreted as “lofty division,” 12.

## THE REPROBATE

They are called for this purpose: that they may be without excuse, 564.

## RESSA

Its name is interpreted as “a praiseworthy temptation,” 12.

## RESURRECTION OF THE FLESH

It is asserted against heretics, 535, 536. Their deceptions, 350. Some attempt to introduce the idea that after the resurrection there will be an airy body, gradually dissolved into thin air, 344. Will there be a difference of sex in the resurrection? 336. Objections by those who deny the resurrection are answered, 337, 341. Will we eat and drink after it? 339. It remains suspended until all who are predestined to life believe, 294. It is the victory of conquered death, 167. Death is from the earth, but resurrection is from heaven—provided that it is transformed for glory, 181. The ungodly will rise, but in order to perish, 167. Unbelief cannot have a clear resurrection, 165. The first and second resurrection, 571.

## RETHMA

That is, “the mouth of the seer,” 12. In its proper name, but together with many other places of the solitude, it is called Pharan, 11. It is the fifteenth encampment of the Israelites, and what happened there? ibid.

## ROME

It is represented by the prostitute, 562, 565. It is called a harlot, 564. Whatever nation among the Romans desired to pursue peace was received, after presenting gifts, so that its people might be Roman citizens, 236. Among the Romans, kings are called Augusti, 82. The power of the Assyrians, Persians, and Macedonians had passed to the Romans, 534, 548. The faith of the Romans is praised, [Col. 1247] 25. The destruction of the Roman Empire is represented, 564. The Romans destroyed the Jews, 560. See ANTICHRIST, DAY OF JUDGMENT.

## RUIN

That which comes from a height strikes with a more severe fall, 360.

# S

## SABELLIUS

He professes that the Father himself is the Son himself, 354. He is a pirate, 453. See ARIUS.

## PRIEST

A priest may be chosen from the people, 242. He is rightly compared with bees, 448. See PRESBYTER.

## SACRAMENT

Christ in the flesh is the sacrament of God’s mystery, 296. The sacraments of spiritual things should not readily be made public, 280.

## SACRIFICE

The holy Church is accustomed to offer a sacrifice of praise to God daily, 500. In the Church, not bodily but spiritual sacrifices are offered daily, 584.

## SALMONA

Its name is interpreted as “shadow,” 17.

## SOLOMON

He differs from the other prophets, and in what respect, 454. It is a fable of certain Jews that Solomon built the Temple with the aid of demons, 316. Why could Solomon not know three impossible things? 451. Those matters are explained, ibid.

## DANCES

Dances before the basilicas of the saints are condemned, 423. Is dancing ever permitted? 447.

## GREETING

The ecclesiastical greeting, 209.

## SALVATION

The necessity of salvation is greater than every other necessity, 443, 444. It is not permissible to be ignorant of what especially pertains to salvation, 199.

## THE SAMARITAN WOMAN

She was taught through the Law, 142.

## SAMARITANS

They are descended from the Persians and Assyrians, 142. They accept only the Law—that is, the five books of Moses—ibid. They worship fire in the Persian manner, ibid.

## SAMUEL

He was sorrowful when Saul sinned, 127.

## SAMSON

He signifies Christ; his hair signifies the elect, 503.

## THE SAINTS

They are kings and priests, and in what way? 519. Who are called “the called saints”? 28. The mind of a saint is engaged in every good, 190. To remember the saints and be a sharer with them means to imitate their actions, 96. Those who minister to the saints make the saints their debtors, 191. “I ask the assistance of Mary, the intercession of the apostles, the prayers of the martyrs, and the supplications of the confessors,” 497.

## THE WISE

Who are called wise? 30. The first part of wisdom is to fear God, 39. What wisdom is so true as to know what is beneficial and despise what is harmful? 267. It acquires life and peace, 71. It is powerful for uprooting every vice, 587. How did it build a house for itself and seven columns? 503. The ancients held that all wise people should be called free, but all imprudent people slaves, 135. Whatever human beings know apart from God is foolish, 123. The wise of this world are in the flesh, 72.

## SARACENS

They conquered all Asia, 564.

## SAREPTA

Its name is interpreted as “burned” or “the distress of bread,” 530.

## SATAN

Its name is interpreted as “adversary,” 588.

## SAUL

He conquered his enemies not so much by weapons as by devotion, and fought more by religion than by arrows, 418. See SAMUEL.

## TO BE SCANDALIZED

Sometimes this means suffering a desire of the flesh, 203.

## SCHOOLS

Teachers are those who were accustomed to instruct children in letters and readings, as is the custom of the Jews. Their tradition passed over to us, but through negligence has grown obsolete, 241.

## KNOWLEDGE

Why is the tree of the knowledge of good and evil so called? 505. Human weakness considers foolish whatever it cannot establish by its own knowledge, 120. Why are astrology, geometry, arithmetic, and music despised by our people? 267. Just as this life is imperfect, so also is knowledge, 155. Knowledge is then great and useful to itself when it is humbled by charity, 138, 139, 140. Supported by charity, it is not puffed up but gentle and beneficial to all, 156. In order to possess a fuller knowledge of things, their principles must first be sought, 25. No one except a good person can possess the knowledge that descends into Christ, 514. The best knowledge is to abandon vices and turn with one’s whole mind toward God, 514.

## SCRIPTURES

It is established that certain Latin manuscripts of Scripture were once translated from ancient Greek copies; the simplicity of the times preserved and attests them as uncorrupted, 56. Many things were changed in them, and by whom, ibid. Why do the Greeks have different copies? 57. To adulterate the word of God is to attempt to exclude the true meaning by means of a false one, 178. This is the priests’ vigorous and abundant vengeance: not to entrust the mysteries of the heavenly Scriptures to any who are unworthy, 464. Divine Scripture always speaks and cries out, 461. The more it is ruminated in the heart, the more healthful sweetness it offers to the mind, 543. It is exceedingly sharp for cutting away vices, 570. It is bread for souls, 529. It is nourishment and life, 429. Some have learned it not out of love for God but out of love for the world, 499. The interpreter of Scripture adds nothing and subtracts nothing, 588. See GOSPEL, TESTAMENT.

## SECURITY

The unwary person lies open to attacks, 597.

## OLD AGE

Among all nations it is honorable, 298. [Col. 1248]

## SEPTUAGESIMA

The Sunday of Septuagesima, a new name, 409. Why is it so called? 410.

## BURIAL

The burial of bodies is arranged by the hands of clerics, 469.

## SERPENT

The serpent suspended on a sign was a type of Christ hanging on the cross for our salvation, 17.

## SLAVES

They are appointed in place of ministers, 123. We are called the slaves of the one whom we obey, 61. It is greater to become a slave from being free than to be born a slave, 227. It is an honor to be the slave of a powerful person, 291. Whoever serves wholeheartedly is outwardly what he is inwardly, 274. Those are suitable slaves who, through their diligence and faith, enlarge their masters’ affairs, 304. A suitable slave is proved to be such when, for love of his master, he offends the master’s enemies, 277. Those are slaves of human beings who subject themselves to human superstitions, 135. “Slave of Christ” is a title of dignity, 274. There is no greater dignity than to serve Christ, 488. The slaves of God serve God by loving and praising him without end, 586. With God, the person who has sinned is considered a slave, 274. People become slaves through sin, 255. See HAM. Sins make slaves, 135.

## SEXAGESIMA

The Sunday of Sexagesima, a new name, 409. Why is it so called? 410.

## SIGNIFICATIONS

The significations of different causes, 269.

## SIMILITUDE

A likeness usually has something unlike, 55.

## SIMPLICITY

Simplicity of conscience and sincerity are a glory, 171.

## SIMON

Simon Magus is said to have flown upward through the air in order to scandalize Christ’s people, 78. He is said to have pretended to die and rise again, 552.

## SIMONY

Ministers who sell ecclesiastical offices are censured, 566.

## DISSEMBLING

Every pretense and every duplicity is a lie, 432.

## SIN

Its name is interpreted as “thorn-bush,” and it is the wilderness extending from the Red Sea to Mount Sinai, 7. The thirty-third encampment in the wilderness of Sin is different from the eighth of the same name, 16.

## SINAI

The twelfth encampment of the Israelites, and what happened there, 9.

## SUCCOTH

The second encampment of the children of Israel, 4. Its name is interpreted as “booths,” ibid. What happened there? ibid.

## ANXIETY

A person becomes more concerned through shame when he sees another suffering in his own cause, 276.

## SOPHISTS

The Greek sophists corrupted Scripture, 215.

## DIVINATION

423.

## HOPE

Where there is no hope, a person must be regarded as dead, 129. Whoever has hope without right faith deceives himself, 521. This is the test of the faithful: whether they direct the hope of their faith toward it, 238. Why have we been liberated through hope? 76. Whoever does anything without hope collapses when tribulation arises, 288. In doubtful hopes, 596, 212, 224.

## SNEEZING

423.

## THE HOLY SPIRIT

Why is he so called? 321. He is proved to be God, 122, 605. This is demonstrated from his gifts, names, works, and effects, 324. He performs everything that God performs, 606. This is proved, 607. Like an image from a ring, and fire from a spark, he is not changed into any of the things he performs, 325. Why is he not the Son? 322. He is from God the Father, 94. From the Father and the Son he proceeds inseparably from eternity, 438, 579, 611. All things belonging to the Father and the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, who belongs to both Father and Son, are common to them, 328. The Holy Spirit is sent by the Son because of the fellowship and unity of nature, 327. He is Christ in substance, 181. Why did he descend upon Christ in the form of a dove? 404. He is signified by fire, 535. Whatever is from God is through God, afterward reborn in the Spirit, 94. How do his seven gifts correspond to each of the faithful? 514. And to Christ? 513. He dwells in believers, 268. He sanctifies the children of God, 244. In those who act well he is shared by God and human beings, 131. He makes petition according to his nature, 76. He is grieved by us and rejoices in us, 103, 244. The person who flees sin walks by the Spirit, 128. The person in whom he is meditates continually on spiritual things, 247. Spiritual things are those which, when preserved, establish merit before God, 212. Whoever despises spiritual things considers them bodily, 195. Just as righteousness makes people spiritual, so offenses make them carnal, 45. See FLESH.

## STARS

Pagans call angels “stars,” 270.

## STEPHEN

For Stephen, the stones of the torrent became sweetness, 6.

## STIPEND

It is what a soldier receives for expenses in place of wages, 199.

## FOOLISH

A person who is wise according to the world is foolish before God, 122.

## SUBSTANCE

Whatever is one in substance is one, 91. Why do we call substance “nature” in God? 257. Those who want to remove the word “substance” introduce the Arian heresy, 348. They are censured, ibid. An objection is answered from heretics who wish entirely to exclude from God the words *homoousion*—“of the same substance”—and “substance,” 351.

## PRIDE

Pride is thinking highly, 97. It is full foolishness if someone praises himself for false things; it is pride if he praises himself for true things, 200. Pride and arrogance are sin, 97. It is the greatest evil, horrible and terrifying, 493. Seven vices arising from it are listed, ibid. It is regarded as a kind of insanity, 183. All the proud are children of the devil, 439. It is wretched for someone to be proud when he does not know what he is, 93. The mind of the proud bears no fruit worthy of God, 182. See ARROGANCE.

## SUPERFLUITIES

They usually produce greater anxiety, 193.

## SUSPICION

It makes a person fearful, 301.

## SUEVI

They laid waste to many places, 564.

## SIBYL

By what spirit did she speak? 119.

## CREED

The creed of the faith, 345. Holy faith was formulated in the creed of the twelve apostles. Like skilled artisans coming together, they forged the key through their deliberation, 435. It is the leaven of our salvation, 408.

## SYMMACHIANS

They derive their origin from the Pharisees and call themselves Christians, 209.

## SYMPHRONIUS

Prefect and persecutor of Agnes, 480 and following.

## SYNAGOGUE

The hand of the synagogue withered in the scribes, teachers, and Pharisees, 411. Why does the Savior heal Adam’s right hand in the synagogue? 412. See CHURCH.

# T

## TELESPHORUS

Pope, 410.

## TEMPTATION

People are tested in different ways: one through poverty and bodily weakness, another through wealth and health, 341. The various tests of believers, 258. Every test is a temptation, but not every temptation is a test, 208. God never allows us to be without either an advocate or a comforter amid the temptations and miseries of this world, 324. Human temptation consists in distrusting a person because of hope in God, 144. The greater and more destructive temptations by which the soul is assaulted in this life are, by universal agreement, judged to be the illusions of demons and the tricks of magicians and diviners, 17. Through the flesh subject to him, the devil introduces evil suggestions into the soul, 69. However perfect the soul may be, unless it is continually seasoned by temptations, it grows lax, 12. Temptation is the soul’s faithful guardianship, strength, and increase of virtue, 15, 18.

## TERMINAL

The final outcome, 603.

## TERTIUS

Tertius, the brother, 192. Tertius, the scribe of Paul’s letter, 110.

## TERTULLIAN

57. He was a man of no small learning, but he created a heresy, 155.

## TESTAMENT

A legally executed testament of a deceased person cannot be broken, 220. The Old Testament is divided by the Hebrews into the Prophets, the Law, and the Hagiographa, 329. It is not contrary to the New Testament, 149. It was a shadow of the New Testament, 542. Spiritual understanding in it is nothing other than the New Testament, 518. Although the New Testament is the disclosure of the Old, many things are nevertheless placed obscurely in it, 532. The New Testament is called a new song, 553. And why is it called “new”? ibid. See GOSPEL, SCRIPTURE.

## TO BE PLACED IN A GLOOMY STATE

165.

## THAATH

In Latin it signifies “long-suffering” or “endurance,” 13.

## THARE

In Latin it is interpreted as “stupor,” in Greek *ekstasis* (ἔκστασις), 13.

## THECLA

She escaped globes of flame, 458.

## FEARS

Various kinds of fear, good and bad, 575. It is a certain sign of admonition to see what one fears, 475. The fear of God should moderate and impose a limit upon incidental causes, 244. Whoever fears is not perfect, 273. Fear restrains sin, 99. It makes one abstain from sins, 273. Fear makes a person whom it corrects more cautious about avoiding past offenses, 602.

## TIMOTHY

Who he was, 289. Because he was the son of a Jewish woman but had a Greek father, he was not circumcised according to the Law, 217. A remarkable young man, 298. And a remarkable man, 305. He was almost Paul’s co-bishop, 110. Paul calls him his son because he had been ordained by him, 257.

## TITUS

He was Greek, 215.

## TOROSUS

The gluttony of the body, 601.

## TRADITION

The apostolic tradition, 347. And that of the Fathers, ibid. Whatever was not handed down by the apostles is full of crimes, 125.

## TRANQUILLITY

In the soul, it is the end of the actions of life, 2.

## PIERCING

The piercing of this life, 243.

## TAXES

Fiscal taxes must be paid, and why? 99.

## TRIBULATIONS

The soul is purified through continual tribulations, 180. Even for those who exist in grace, many bitter tribulations remain, 6. Why should one glory in tribulations? 52. Tribulation is the sign of fixed hope, which bears witness to the crown, 52. See ADVERSITY.

## THE TRINITY

The mystery of the Trinity, 492. It is truth, 117. The term “Holy Trinity” is a great mystery and an arcane reality, 329. This alone is what we understand about the Trinity: that it cannot be understood, 322. What should one think about it? 321. The mystery of the Trinity is proved from the Apostle, 605. We believe that the three names and three persons in the Trinity are of one essence, one majesty, and one power, 347. There is both unity in the Trinity and Trinity in unity, 324. The mystery of the Trinity [Col. 1250] is enclosed within the nature and power of the one God, although it is immeasurable, 151. The Father is of the same nature as the Son, and he is in the Holy Spirit, 94. Let us understand the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit as each existing in his own subsistence, 322. The Father and Son are one power, one divinity, and one substance, 287. Between the Father and the Holy Spirit there is a distinction of persons, not of nature, 239, 293. Between the Son of God and the Father there is not union but distinction of persons, 77. Although the Father and Son are believed to be two persons, they are nevertheless one in reason and substance, 353. The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are one in dominion, one in divinity, and one in omnipotence, 517. There is always one worship, one veneration, one adoration, and one sanctification of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, 323. Since it is established that the Father and Son are of one substance, each is called one God, 354. Whoever does not doubt concerning the second person of the Trinity also accepts the third, 280. It is necessary that the person of the Father be placed first, 183. The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are shown to be without beginning, 323, 325. Eternity is in the Father, expression in the image, and use in the gift, 321. How appropriately are the Father called “voice” and the Son “Word”? 404. Whatever the Father speaks is the word of the Son and the Holy Spirit, and conversely, 327. The holy and inseparable Trinity never performs anything outside itself, 326. All things were created from the Father but through the Son, 139. When John says, “I and the Father are one,” “one” refers to the unity of divinity, while “are” assigns the distinction of persons, 347. The whole sum of perfection consists in the Trinity, 173. See SON.

## SADNESS

What vices does it generate? 494. Whoever is sad because he has sinned is sad according to God, 189.

# U

## URSICINUS

His martyrdom, 485.

## UTENSILS

Those belonging to another, 300. To provide the utensils of the saints for their needs, 217.

## WIFE

No one is blessed with a second wife, 295. See MARRIAGE, MATRIMONY.

# V

## WOMB

The Holy Spirit did not disdain the human womb, 340.

## VALENS AND URSACIUS

453.

## VALERIA

Mother of the most blessed Gervasius and Protasius, 485. Her martyrdom, ibid.

## VANDALS

They claimed Africa for themselves, 564.

## VANITY

The worship of idols, 246.

## WORDS

They come after things, 117. Whoever does not restrain an idle word quickly proceeds to harmful ones, 488.

## TRUTH

It endures through everlasting ages, 238. That is true which is eternal, 313. What is truth except life? 292. Nothing is so public as truth, 100. Whatever is true cannot be dishonorable, 315. Whatever true thing is said by anyone is said by the Holy Spirit, 150. Whatever is set against the truth is a human invention, 314.

## GARMENTS

To shine in clothing while being filthy with crimes is of no benefit, 393. It is much better to adorn the soul with virtues than to clothe the body in precious garments, 391.

## VICTORINUS

57.

## WIDOW

Which widow should be admitted to the Church’s stipends? 299. And so that her name may be entered in the ecclesiastical records, ibid. How greatly do even widows who were wives of two or three husbands burden the Church? 300.

## WATCHFULNESS

We are accustomed to be more attentive in the affairs of others, 75.

## TO BE CONQUERED

No one tolerates being conquered, 308. It is customary for a palm to be offered to the victors, 433.

## VENGEANCE

If vengeance is left to God, one benefits in two ways, 98.

## MAN

See MATRIMONY.

## VIRGIN

The glorious title of virgin and widow, 300. Nothing is so excellent and useful as virginity, 135. A person may be a virgin in body but corrupted in mind, 366. What does it profit to be a virgin in body if the mind happens to be corrupted? 495. A consecrated virgin who has publicly professed virginity is warned away from the use and association of secular men, 365 and following. Virgins ought to refuse gifts offered by men under the appearance of piety, 457. God will not count as holiness in those who think about the world, 137. See CONSTANCY.

## VIRTUE

The beautiful order and happy progress of virtue, which always tends toward better things, 6. We must be fortified by three strongholds—faith, hope, and charity—and why? 282. Whoever is humble, obedient, merciful, and patient must be renewed daily so that, by progressing, he may grow in virtues, 409. To pass by what is permitted is the greatest virtue, and not to desire what is forbidden [Col. 1251] is not far removed from it, 136. Undiscerning virtue is counted as vice, 489.

## LIFE

This life is not repose but continual transition, 16. There are four lives of the faithful, 572. There are two lives, active and contemplative, 504, 583. See CONTEMPLATIVE. Life is to know God through Christ, 60. Whoever lives for God by acting well truly lives, 60, ibid. God came and dwelt in human beings in order to give mortals an honorable manner of living, 437. How did Christ make known to us the ways of life? 474. A good and chaste life must be adorned with good morals and enriched with benevolence, 229. Through a good life the hope of faith is obtained, 94. This is eternal life: to live without punishment and to possess glory, 130. Eternal life is equal for all, 472. An evil life corrupts the whole person, 128.

## VITALINUS

See MAIANUS.

## VITALIS

Father of the most blessed Gervasius and Protasius, 485. His martyrdom, ibid. The martyrdom of Vitalis and Agricola and the discovery of their bodies are described, 487.

## VICES

Demons are more easily endured than vices, 550. [Col. 1252] Whoever serves vices worships the image of the beast, 559.

## TO CALL

To call is to assist someone thinking about faith, or to prick the conscience of someone whom one knows to be listening, 77, 82. Who are called according to purpose? 76.

## WILL

What is done willingly is done better, 142. A thing that is not done spontaneously does not reach completion, 283. Once the impediment has been removed, the will restores itself through stronger virtue, 133. A person does not live for himself if he is prepared to do the will of his master, 183. In Scripture, “will” is often used for “threat,” 526.

## PLEASURE

To secular people nothing seems so harmless and agreeable as pleasure, 65.

## VOWS

Let us vow faithfully; God will grant the ability to fulfill them, 395.

# Z

## ZEAL

Nothing consumes a person as zeal does, 88. Every quarrel and zeal produces hostility, 100. [Col. 1251]

## Notice concerning the letters separated from the number of the Ambrosian letters. 733

# LETTERS SEPARATED FROM THE NUMBER OF THE AMBROSIAN LETTERS. 735

## LETTER I.—Before the martyrdom of the virgin Agnes is described, the love of the prefect’s son for her and her rejection of him are recalled. There follows the virgin’s condemnation to a brothel, and, among the miracles divinely performed on behalf of the same girl, the death of the young man who was desperately in love with her and his restoration to life. Then follows the virgin’s condemnation to the stake on account of a pagan uprising, and her bloody execution while she remained unharmed amid the flames. Soon afterward, the fury of the pagans against the Christians who were persisting in prayer at the martyr’s tomb is described; the death of Emerentiana and the restoration of the health of the Empress Constantia are recounted, as well as the temple built by that princess to her liberator and her own resolve of virginity together with that of several others. 735

## LETTER II.—Since God’s benefits ought not to be concealed, he relates a vision in which, during Lent, Gervasius and Protasius appeared to him once and again, and on the third occasion Paul also appeared, commanding him to build a church for them after their relics had been exhumed. He adds that, after his fellow bishops had been summoned, the bodies of the saints were found; from a document discovered there he reports their conversion, death, and burial. The martyrdom of Vitalis and Valeria is also inserted into this account. 743

## LETTER III.—He relates the discovery, amid the applause of the Christians, the amazement of the Jews, and not a few miracles, of the martyrs Vitalis and Agricola, who had been buried at Bologna among the tombs of the Jews. He praises them both for their name and for their steadfastness under punishments, and adds several other matters pertaining to the same subject. 747

## LETTER IV.—Urging Florianus to mature and continual repentance, he prescribes what ought to be followed or avoided by him, whether in words or in deeds. [Column 1254] 749
